    {

      "id": "GHSA-cgm6-wvp9-4g5h",

      "aliases": [
        "CVE-2026-13318"
      ],
      "details": "A server-side request forgery (SSRF) flaw was found in KubeVirt's virt-api port-forward handler. When processing a port-forward request to a VirtualMachineInstance (VMI), virt-api reads the target IP from vmi.Status.Interfaces[0].IP and passes it directly to net.Dial() without validation. For VMIs using non-masquerade network bindings (bridge or secondary-only), this IP is reported by the QEMU guest agent running inside the VM and is fully controllable by the VM owner. An attacker with kubevirt.io:edit permissions can create a VM with a modified guest agent that reports an arbitrary IP address, then request port-forward to establish a bidirectional TCP tunnel from virt-api's cluster-internal network position to any routable destination, bypassing NetworkPolicy isolation.",
      "severity": [
        {
          "type": "CVSS_V3",
          "score": "CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:L/I:L/A:N"
        }
      ],

      ],
      "details": "A flaw was found in KubeVirt's downward metrics virtio-serial server. The server reads guest requests using textproto.Reader.ReadLine(), which buffers input indefinitely until a newline character is received, with no length limit or read deadline. A user with access to a VM guest that has the downward metrics virtio-serial device configured can write a continuous byte stream to the device, causing unbounded memory allocation in the virt-handler process until it is OOM-killed.",

        "CVE-2026-6329"
      ],
      "details": "PKCS#12 MAC verification uses an attacker-controlled comparison length, weakening the integrity check on the MAC and allowing a mismatched MAC to be accepted. The PKCS#12 verify path compared the locally computed HMAC against the MAC parsed from the PKCS#12 structure using a length taken directly from the attacker-supplied input, without first verifying that it equals the length of the digest actually produced by the configured algorithm. A truncated or zero-length stored MAC could therefore be accepted, defeating the integrity protection of the MAC.",
      "severity": [

    {
      "schema_version": "1.4.0",
      "id": "GHSA-gq94-hf88-g4wv",
      "modified": "2026-06-26T00:32:06Z",
      "published": "2026-06-26T00:32:06Z",
      "aliases": [
        "CVE-2026-55962"
      ],
      "details": "TLS 1.3 post-handshake authentication (PHA) issue where a server could accept a client's Finished message without the client having sent a Certificate and CertificateVerify. The post-handshake-auth exemption that allows an empty/absent peer certificate was only intended for the initial handshake, but it was also being applied while a post-handshake CertificateRequest was still outstanding. The check is now scoped to the initial handshake only: on the server, once a post-handshake CertificateRequest has been sent (certReqCtx is set), a peer certificate and a valid CertificateVerify are required again before the Finished is accepted, with empty-certificate handling following the configured verify mode (FAIL_IF_NO_PEER_CERT) just as during first-handshake client authentication. Only affects TLS 1.3 servers built with post-handshake authentication support (WOLFSSL_POST_HANDSHAKE_AUTH / --enable-postauth, included in --enable-all) that enable WOLFSSL_VERIFY_POST_HANDSHAKE and request a client certificate after the handshake via wolfSSL_request_certificate(). Clients, and servers that do not use post-handshake authentication, are unaffected.",
      "severity": [
        {
          "type": "CVSS_V4",
          "score": "CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:L/UI:N/VC:N/VI:H/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N/E:X/CR:X/IR:X/AR:X/MAV:X/MAC:X/MAT:X/MPR:X/MUI:X/MVC:X/MVI:X/MVA:X/MSC:X/MSI:X/MSA:X/S:X/AU:X/R:X/V:X/RE:X/U:X"

      "aliases": [
        "CVE-2026-6331"
      ],
      "details": "HMAC zero-length tag forgery in EVP_DigestVerifyFinal, where a zero-length tag could be accepted as valid during HMAC verification. In the OpenSSL-compatibility HMAC verify path the supplied signature length was only checked as not exceeding the MAC length, so a zero-length or otherwise truncated tag could pass verification. The fix requires the supplied tag length to exactly equal the MAC length and rejects a zero-length MAC, so a forged short or empty tag is no longer accepted.",
      "severity": [
        {
          "type": "CVSS_V4",
          "score": "CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:H/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:L/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N/E:X/CR:X/IR:X/AR:X/MAV:X/MAC:X/MAT:X/MPR:X/MUI:X/MVC:X/MVI:X/MVA:X/MSC:X/MSI:X/MSA:X/S:X/AU:X/R:X/V:X/RE:X/U:X"

        "CVE-2026-8720"
      ],
      "details": "wc_Blake2bHmacFinal and wc_Blake2sHmacFinal discard the message when the key length exceeds the block size, producing a MAC that is independent of the input. When the supplied key is longer than the BLAKE2 block size the key-hashing branch reinitialized the running hash state, discarding the accumulated message data, so the resulting MAC depended only on the key and not on the message being authenticated. This bug is specific to the HMAC-BLAKE2 APIs that were added in wolfSSL version 5.9.0.",
      "severity": [

        "CVE-2026-10098"
      ],
      "details": "OCSP CertID serial-number length-confusion in wolfSSL_OCSP_resp_find_status allows a same-issuer SingleResponse whose serial is a prefix of the target serial to be reported as the revocation status of a different certificate. The lookup compared serial-number bytes without first requiring the two serial numbers to be of equal length, so a SingleResponse for one certificate (same issuer) whose serial is a prefix of the target's serial would match, returning the wrong certificate's status. The fix requires the serial lengths to be equal before comparing the serial bytes.",
      "severity": [
        {
          "type": "CVSS_V4",

      "aliases": [
        "CVE-2025-71336"
      ],
      "details": "Flowise before 3.0.6 (affected versions 2.2.7-patch.1 and earlier) contains an unsandboxed remote code execution vulnerability in the Custom MCP feature, which is designed to execute OS commands such as launching local MCP servers. Because Flowise's authentication and authorization model is minimal and lacks role-based access control, and the default installation runs without authentication unless FLOWISE_USERNAME and FLOWISE_PASSWORD are set, an attacker can send a crafted JSON payload with the header 'x-request-from: internal' to the /api/v1/node-load-method/customMCP endpoint to execute arbitrary OS commands, resulting in complete compromise of the platform container or server.",
      "severity": [
        {
          "type": "CVSS_V3",
          "score": "CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H"
        },

        "CVE-2025-71340"
      ],
      "details": "picklescan through 0.0.26 fails to detect malicious pickle files that invoke idlelib.pyshell.ModifiedInterpreter.runcode in __reduce__ methods. Attackers can embed undetected code in pickle files that executes arbitrary commands when the file is loaded via pickle.load(), enabling supply chain attacks on PyTorch models and saved Python objects. This is fixed in version 0.0.30.",
      "severity": [
        {
          "type": "CVSS_V3",
          "score": "CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N"
        },

\n\n\n\n\n
Acupuncture Used as Weapon to Fight Opioids\n

            "senderName": "NWS Amarillo TX",
            "headline": "Special Weather Statement issued June 25 at 8:50PM CDT by NWS Amarillo TX",
            "description": "At 850 PM CDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm 4\nmiles south of Briscoe, or 21 miles north of Shamrock, moving east at\n30 mph.\n\nHAZARD...Wind gusts of 50 to 55 mph and penny size hail.\n\nSOURCE...Radar indicated.\n\nIMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around\nunsecured objects. Minor hail damage to vegetation is\npossible.\n\nLocations impacted include...\nBriscoe, Wheeler, Allison, New Mobeetie, and Mobeetie.",
            "instruction": "If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.\n\nTorrential rainfall is also occurring with this storm and may lead to\nlocalized flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded\nroadways.\n\nA Severe Thunderstorm Watch remains in effect until 1100 PM CDT for\nthe Panhandle of Texas.",

            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Amarillo TX",
            "headline": "Flash Flood Warning issued June 25 at 8:50PM CDT until June 25 at 10:45PM CDT by NWS Amarillo TX",
            "description": "FFWAMA\n\nThe National Weather Service in Amarillo has issued a\n\n* Flash Flood Warning for...\nSoutheastern Hemphill County in the panhandle of Texas...\nNorthern Wheeler County in the panhandle of Texas...\n\n* Until 1045 PM CDT.\n\n* At 850 PM CDT, the public reported thunderstorms producing heavy\nrain in Wheeler, TX. The expected rainfall rate is 1.5 to 2 inches\nin 1 hour. Flash flooding is already occurring.\n\nHAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.\n\nSOURCE...Public reported.\n\nIMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban\nareas, highways, streets and underpasses as well as\nother poor drainage and low-lying areas.\n\n* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...\nBriscoe, Wheeler, Allison, New Mobeetie and Mobeetie.",
            "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nBe especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the\ndangers of flooding.\n\nBe aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.\n\nRemain alert for flooding even in locations not receiving rain.\nArroyos, streams, and rivers can become raging killer currents in a\nmatter of minutes, even from distant rainfall.",
            "response": "Avoid",
            "note": null,

            "senderName": "NWS Cleveland OH",
            "headline": "Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued June 25 at 9:50PM EDT until June 25 at 10:45PM EDT by NWS Cleveland OH",
            "description": "SVRCLE\n\nThe National Weather Service in Cleveland has issued a\n\n* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...\nNortheastern Ashtabula County in northeastern Ohio...\nSouthern Erie County in northwestern Pennsylvania...\nNorthwestern Crawford County in northwestern Pennsylvania...\n\n* Until 1045 PM EDT.\n\n* At 950 PM EDT, a severe thunderstorm was located 13 miles northwest\nof Girard, or 15 miles north of Conneaut, moving southeast at 30\nmph.\n\nHAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.\n\nSOURCE...Radar indicated.\n\nIMPACT...Minor damage to vehicles is possible. Expect damage to\ntrees and power lines.\n\n* Locations impacted include...\nErie, Conneaut, Edinboro, Girard, Waterford, Albion, Lake City,\nCranesville, Springboro, Platea, McKean, and Avonia.",
            "instruction": "For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a\nbuilding.\n\nIf on Lake Erie, get away from the water and move indoors or inside\na vehicle. Remember, lightning can strike out to 15 miles from the\nparent thunderstorm. If you can hear thunder, you are close enough\nto be struck by lightning. Move to safe shelter now!  Do not be\ncaught on the water in a thunderstorm.",
            "response": "Shelter",
            "note": null,

            "senderName": "NWS Springfield MO",
            "headline": "Flood Watch issued June 25 at 8:47PM CDT by NWS Springfield MO",
            "description": "...The Flood Watch is extended for the following rivers in\nMissouri...\n\nOsage River at Taberville affecting St. Clair zone.\n\nFor the Osage River...including Taberville...flooding is possible.\n\n* WHAT...Flooding is possible.\n\n* WHERE...Osage River at Taberville.\n\n* WHEN...From Sunday evening until further notice.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 23.3 feet, The handicapped access to the Osage River\nlaunch near Taberville floods.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 7:45 PM CDT Thursday the stage was 17.5 feet.\n- Forecast...Flood stage may be reached late Sunday evening.\n- Flood stage is 23.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "If you are in the watch area, remain alert to possible flooding.\n\nResidents and those with interests near the river should monitor\nrising water levels and be prepared for possible flood warnings.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.\n\nThe next statement will be issued Friday morning at 1000 AM CDT.",
            "response": "Prepare",
            "note": null,

            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Lincoln IL",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 25 at 8:47PM CDT by NWS Lincoln IL",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in\nIllinois...\n\nIllinois River at Henry affecting Putnam and Marshall Counties.\n\n...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in\nIllinois...\n\nIllinois River at Peoria affecting Woodford, Peoria and Tazewell\nCounties.\n\nIllinois River at Beardstown affecting Morgan, Brown, Schuyler\nand Cass Counties.\n\nIllinois River near Havana affecting Mason, Cass and Fulton\nCounties.\n\n.The following forecasts are based on observed precipitation, soil\nmoisture conditions, and forecast precipitation.\n\n* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is\nforecast.\n\n* WHERE...Illinois River near Havana.\n\n* WHEN...Until further notice.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 19.5 feet, Access road to Anderson Lake north\ncampground closed.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 7:45 PM CDT Thursday the stage was 19.8 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours\nending at 7:45 PM CDT Thursday was 19.8 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to fall to 17.4 feet\nThursday, July 02.\n- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Persons with interests along this river need to remain aware of the\nlatest forecasts and associated flood risk for their area. Stay\ntuned for further updates on this flooding situation.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.",
            "response": "Avoid",
            "note": null,

            "senderName": "NWS St Louis MO",
            "headline": "Flood Advisory issued June 25 at 8:47PM CDT until June 26 at 12:45AM CDT by NWS St Louis MO",
            "description": "* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.\n\n* WHERE...Randolph County in southwestern Illinois...\n\n* WHEN...Until 1245 AM CDT.\n\n* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 847 PM CDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to\nthunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin\nshortly in the advisory area. Between 1 and 3 inches of rain have\nfallen.\n- Some locations that will experience flooding include...\nChester, Sparta, Red Bud, Bremen, Steeleville, Percy,\nCoulterville, Tilden, Evansville, Baldwin, Eden, Preston, Blair,\nPrairie Du Rocher, Prairie, Ellis Grove, Ruma and Houston.",
            "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nBe especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the\ndangers of flooding.",
            "response": "Avoid",
            "note": null,

            "headline": "Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued June 25 at 7:47PM MDT until June 25 at 8:15PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM",
            "description": "SVRABQ\n\nThe National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a\n\n* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...\nCentral Chaves County in southeastern New Mexico...\n\n* Until 815 PM MDT.\n\n* At 747 PM MDT, a severe thunderstorm was located near Roswell,\nmoving northeast at 25 mph.\n\nHAZARD...60 mph wind gusts.\n\nSOURCE...Surface observations.\n\nIMPACT...Expect damage to roofs, siding, and trees.\n\n* Locations impacted include...\nRoswell, Bitter Lake Wildlife Refuge, Bottomless Lakes State Park\nand Midway.\n\nThis includes the following highways...\nHighway 380 between Mile Markers 156 and 172. Highway 285 between\nMile Markers 99 and 104.",
            "instruction": "Seek shelter inside a well-built structure and stay away from\nwindows. This storm has produced damaging winds.\n\nBlowing dust associated with strong thunderstorm winds can reduce\nvisibility below one quarter mile at times.",

            "senderName": "NWS Lincoln IL",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 25 at 8:47PM CDT by NWS Lincoln IL",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in\nIllinois...\n\nIllinois River at Henry affecting Putnam and Marshall Counties.\n\n...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in\nIllinois...\n\nIllinois River at Peoria affecting Woodford, Peoria and Tazewell\nCounties.\n\nIllinois River at Beardstown affecting Morgan, Brown, Schuyler\nand Cass Counties.\n\nIllinois River near Havana affecting Mason, Cass and Fulton\nCounties.\n\n.The following forecasts are based on observed precipitation, soil\nmoisture conditions, and forecast precipitation.\n\n* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is\nforecast.\n\n* WHERE...Illinois River at Beardstown.\n\n* WHEN...Until further notice.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 20.0 feet, Seepage problems begin in the South\nBeardstown Drainage and Levee District.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 7:45 PM CDT Thursday the stage was 21.2 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours\nending at 7:45 PM CDT Thursday was 21.2 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 21.5\nfeet early Saturday afternoon.\n- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Persons with interests along this river need to remain aware of the\nlatest forecasts and associated flood risk for their area. Stay\ntuned for further updates on this flooding situation.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.",
            "response": "Avoid",

            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 25 at 8:47PM CDT until June 29 at 7:00AM CDT by NWS Lincoln IL",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in\nIllinois...\n\nIllinois River at Henry affecting Putnam and Marshall Counties.\n\n...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in\nIllinois...\n\nIllinois River at Peoria affecting Woodford, Peoria and Tazewell\nCounties.\n\nIllinois River at Beardstown affecting Morgan, Brown, Schuyler\nand Cass Counties.\n\nIllinois River near Havana affecting Mason, Cass and Fulton\nCounties.\n\n.The following forecasts are based on observed precipitation, soil\nmoisture conditions, and forecast precipitation.\n\n* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is\nforecast.\n\n* WHERE...Illinois River at Henry.\n\n* WHEN...Until Monday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 23.0 feet, Water begins to affect the marina in Henry\nalong with minor flooding of land adjacent to the river.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 7:45 PM CDT Thursday the stage was 24.0 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours\nending at 7:45 PM CDT Thursday was 24.2 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage\nearly Monday morning and continue falling to 21.3 feet\nThursday, July 02.\n- Flood stage is 23.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Persons with interests along this river need to remain aware of the\nlatest forecasts and associated flood risk for their area. Stay\ntuned for further updates on this flooding situation.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.",

            "headline": "Small Craft Advisory issued June 25 at 9:45PM EDT until June 26 at 4:00AM EDT by NWS Wakefield VA",
            "description": "* WHAT...South winds 15 to 20 kt with gusts up to 25 kt and\nwaves 2 to 3 ft expected.\n\n* WHERE...Chesapeake Bay from Smith Point to Windmill Point VA,\nChesapeake Bay from Windmill Point to New Point Comfort VA,\nChesapeake Bay from New Point Comfort to Little Creek VA and\nChesapeake Bay from Little Creek VA to Cape Henry VA including\nthe Chesapeake Bay Bridge Tunnel.\n\n* WHEN...Until 4 AM EDT Friday.\n\n* IMPACTS...Conditions will be hazardous to small craft.",

            "event": "Flood Warning",
            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Lincoln IL",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 25 at 8:45PM CDT until July 1 at 9:24PM CDT by NWS Lincoln IL",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in\nIllinois...\n\nEmbarras River at Lawrenceville affecting Lawrence County.\n\n.The following forecasts are based on observed precipitation, soil\nmoisture conditions, and forecast precipitation.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Embarras River at Lawrenceville.\n\n* WHEN...Until late Wednesday evening.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 36.0 feet, Billet-Vincennes River road is inundated.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 7:45 PM CDT Thursday the stage was 32.5 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours\nending at 7:45 PM CDT Thursday was 32.5 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 34.8\nfeet Sunday morning. It will then fall below flood stage\nWednesday afternoon.\n- Flood stage is 30.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Persons with interests along this river need to remain aware of the\nlatest forecasts and associated flood risk for their area. Stay\ntuned for further updates on this flooding situation.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.",
            "response": "Avoid",
            "note": null,

            "senderName": "NWS Cleveland OH",
            "headline": "Special Marine Warning issued June 25 at 9:44PM EDT until June 25 at 10:30PM EDT by NWS Cleveland OH",
            "description": "For the following areas...\nNearshore and Open waters from Geneva-on-the-lake OH to Ripley NY...\n\nAt 943 PM EDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing waterspouts\nwas located 13 nm north of Conneaut, moving southeast at 25 knots.\n\nHAZARD...Waterspouts, wind gusts 34 knots or greater, and small\nhail.\n\nSOURCE...Radar indicated.\n\nIMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally\nhazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly\nhigher winds and suddenly higher waves.\n\nLocations impacted include...\nErie and Conneaut.",
            "instruction": "Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily\noverturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor\nimmediately.",
            "response": "Avoid",

            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 25 at 8:44PM CDT until June 29 at 3:24PM CDT by NWS Tulsa OK",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in\nOklahoma...\n\nNeosho River near Commerce affecting Ottawa County.\n\nSpring River near Quapaw affecting Ottawa County.\n\n* WHAT...Moderate flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Neosho River near Commerce.\n\n* WHEN...From Friday evening to Monday afternoon.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 20.0 feet, moderate agricultural flooding occurs.\nRiverview Park experiences moderate flooding.             "headline": "Special Weather Statement issued June 25 at 7:43PM MDT by NWS Glasgow MT",
            "description": "At 741 PM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm near\nU L Bend Rec Area, or 38 miles northeast of Winnett, moving northeast\nat 20 mph.\n\nHAZARD...Winds in excess of 40 mph and half inch hail.\n\nSOURCE...Radar indicated.\n\nIMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around\nunsecured objects. Minor damage to outdoor objects is\npossible.\n\nLocations impacted include...\nDevils Creek Rec Area, Crooked Creek Rec Area, and U L Bend Rec Area.",
            "instruction": "If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.\n\nTorrential rainfall is also occurring with this storm and may lead to\nlocalized flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded\nroadways.\n\nIf on or near Fort Peck Lake, get out of the water and move indoors\nor inside a vehicle. Remember, lightning can strike out to 10 miles\nfrom the parent thunderstorm. If you can hear thunder, you are close\nenough to be struck by lightning. Move to safe shelter now!             "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Springfield MO",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 25 at 8:43PM CDT until June 29 at 5:37PM CDT by NWS Springfield MO",
            "description": "...The National Weather Service in Springfield MO has issued a Flood\nWarning for the following rivers in Missouri...\n\nMarmaton River near Nevada affecting Vernon County.\n\nFor the Marmaton River...including Nevada...Minor flooding is\nforecast.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Marmaton River near Nevada.\n\n* WHEN...From Friday afternoon to Monday afternoon.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 26.0 feet, moderate flooding occurs at the gage site.\nFlood waters affect the Old U.S. Highway 71 Bridge North of Nevada\nand the south bound lane of Highway 71 near the junction of\nDouglas Branch and the Marmaton River.\n\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 7:45 PM CDT Thursday the stage was 7.5 feet.\n- Bankfull stage is 20.0 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage\ntomorrow afternoon to a crest of 25.6 feet Saturday evening.\nIt will then fall below flood stage late Monday morning.\n- Flood stage is 20.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Many flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.\n\nThe next statement will be issued Friday morning at 1000 AM CDT.",
            "response": "Avoid",

            "headline": "Special Weather Statement issued June 25 at 7:42PM MDT by NWS Billings MT",
            "description": "At 742 PM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking a line of strong\nthunderstorms extending from 21 miles north of Laurel to 8 miles\nnorthwest of Laurel, or extending from 20 miles northwest of Billings\nto 15 miles west of Billings, moving east at 15 mph.\n\nHAZARD...Wind gusts up to 40 to 50 mph and pea size hail.\n\nSOURCE...Radar indicated.\n\nIMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around\nunsecured objects. Minor damage to outdoor objects is\npossible.\n\nLocations impacted include...\nBillings, Billings West End, Billings Heights, Acton, Comanche and\nMolt.",
            "instruction": "Monitor the weather situation closely and be alert for threatening\nweather conditions.\n\nTorrential rainfall is also occurring with these storms and may lead\nto flash flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded\nroadways.",

            "senderName": "NWS Springfield MO",
            "headline": "Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued June 25 at 8:41PM CDT until June 25 at 9:45PM CDT by NWS Springfield MO",
            "description": "SVRSGF\n\nThe National Weather Service in Springfield has issued a\n\n* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...\nEastern Cherokee County in southeastern Kansas...\nSoutheastern Crawford County in southeastern Kansas...\n\n* Until 945 PM CDT.\n\n* At 841 PM CDT, a severe thunderstorm was located near Cherokee, or\n10 miles south of Girard, moving southeast at 25 mph.\n\nHAZARD...Golf ball size hail and 60 mph wind gusts.\n\nSOURCE...Radar indicated.\n\nIMPACT...People and animals outdoors will be injured. Expect hail\ndamage to roofs, siding, windows, and vehicles. Expect\nwind damage to roofs, siding, and trees.\n\n* Locations impacted include...\nPittsburg, Frontenac, Columbus, Galena, Cherokee, Weir, Lowell,\nScammon, Chicopee, Roseland, Neutral, Opolis, Riverton, Lawton,\nCarona, Lone Oak, Skidmore, Stippville, and Crestline.\n\nThis includes Interstate 44 near mile marker 0.",
            "instruction": "For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a\nbuilding.\n\nTorrential rainfall is occurring with this storm, and may lead to\nflash flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded roadways.",

            "description": "At 741 PM MDT, a severe thunderstorm was located 8 miles south of Des\nMoines, moving southeast at 20 mph.\n\nHAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.\n\nSOURCE...Public reported.\n\nIMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind damage to\nroofs, siding, and trees.\n\nLocations impacted include...\nDes Moines and Capulin.\n\nThis includes Highway 64 between Mile Markers 376 and 394.",
            "instruction": "Seek shelter inside a well-built structure and stay away from\nwindows. This storm is capable of producing damaging winds and has\nproduced large hail.",

            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Springfield MO",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 25 at 8:40PM CDT until June 27 at 2:39AM CDT by NWS Springfield MO",
            "description": "...The National Weather Service in Springfield MO has issued a Flood\nWarning for the following rivers in Kansas...\n\nMarmaton River at Fort Scott affecting Bourbon County.\n\nFor the Marmaton River...including Fort Scott...Minor flooding is\nforecast.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Marmaton River at Fort Scott.\n\n* WHEN...From Friday evening to early Saturday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 38.0 feet, minor flooding begins along Mill Creek\nnorth of town due to backwater effects of the Marmaton River.\nFlood waters also spill across the field by the Red Barn\nRestaurant, on the north side of town, at the new Highway 69\nBridge.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 7:30 PM CDT Thursday the stage was 11.1 feet.\n- Bankfull stage is 38.0 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage to\na crest of 38.3 feet tomorrow evening. It will then fall\nbelow flood stage tomorrow evening.\n- Flood stage is 38.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Many flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.\n\nThe next statement will be issued Friday morning at 1000 AM CDT.",
            "response": "Avoid",
            "note": null,

            "headline": "Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued June 25 at 8:40PM CDT until June 25 at 9:45PM CDT by NWS Wichita KS",
            "description": "SVRICT\n\nThe National Weather Service in Wichita has issued a\n\n* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...\nNorthwestern Labette County in southeastern Kansas...\nNortheastern Montgomery County in southeastern Kansas...\n\n* Until 945 PM CDT.\n\n* At 840 PM CDT, a severe thunderstorm was located 2\nmiles north of Cherryvale, moving east at 15 mph.\n\nHAZARD...Half dollar size hail.\n\nSOURCE...Radar indicated.\n\nIMPACT...Damage to vehicles is expected.\n\n* Locations impacted include...\nParsons, Cherryvale, Altamont, Mound Valley, Parsons Tri City\nAirport, Dennis, and Big Hill Lake.",
            "instruction": "For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a\nbuilding.\n\nTorrential rainfall is occurring with this storm, and may lead to\nflash flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded roadways.",

            "description": "SMWBUF\n\nThe National Weather Service in Buffalo has issued a\n\n* Special Marine Warning for...\nLake Erie from Ripley to east of Dunkirk...\n\n* Until 1115 PM EDT.\n\n* At 939 PM EDT, severe thunderstorms were located along a line\nextending from 22 nm northwest of Ripley to near Erie, moving\nnortheast at 25 knots.\n\nHAZARD...Wind gusts to 40 knots and large hail.\n\nSOURCE...Radar.\n\nIMPACT...Small craft could be damaged in briefly higher winds and\nsuddenly higher waves. Large hail could result in\nstructural damage.\n\n* Locations impacted include...\nVan Buren Point, Dunkirk, Barcelona, and Ripley.",
            "instruction": "Move to safe harbor immediately as gusty winds and high waves are\nexpected.\n\nFrequent lightning is occurring with these storms. If caught on the\nopen water stay below deck if possible, keep away from ungrounded\nmetal objects.",
            "response": "Avoid",
            "note": null,

            "senderName": "NWS Springfield MO",
            "headline": "Flash Flood Warning issued June 25 at 8:40PM CDT until June 26 at 2:45AM CDT by NWS Springfield MO",
            "description": "FFWSGF\n\nThe National Weather Service in Springfield has issued a\n\n* Flash Flood Warning for...\nNorthwestern Cherokee County in southeastern Kansas...\nSouthern Crawford County in southeastern Kansas...\n\n* Until 245 AM CDT Friday.\n\n* At 840 PM CDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing\nheavy rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain\nhave fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 1.5 to 3 inches in 1\nhour. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.\n\nHAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.\n\nSOURCE...Radar.\n\nIMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban\nareas, highways, streets and underpasses as well as\nother poor drainage and low-lying areas.\n\n* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...\nGirard, Arma, Cherokee, Mccune, Walnut, West Mineral, Roseland,\nGreenbush, Beulah, Brazilton, Carona, Ringo and Polk.",
            "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Many flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nBe especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the\ndangers of flooding.",
            "response": "Avoid",
            "note": null,

            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in\nOklahoma...\n\nCaney River near Collinsville affecting Tulsa and Rogers Counties.\n\nCaney River near Ramona affecting Washington OK County.\n\nCaney River at Bartlesville affecting Washington OK County.\n\n* WHAT...Moderate flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Caney River near Ramona.\n\n* WHEN...From late tonight to early Sunday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 28.0 feet, moderate agricultural flooding occurs from\nOchelata to the northeastern tip of Tulsa County. Some rural roads\nare impassable including the road between Ramona and Talala.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 7:57 PM CDT Thursday the stage was 20.8 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage\njust after midnight tonight to a crest of 28.5 feet tomorrow\nevening.             "headline": "Special Weather Statement issued June 25 at 8:39PM CDT by NWS Paducah KY",
            "description": "At 839 PM CDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm over\nVienna, moving northeast at 15 mph.\n\nHAZARD...Wind gusts up to 50 mph and half inch hail.\n\nSOURCE...Radar indicated.\n\nIMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around\nunsecured objects. Minor hail damage to vegetation is\npossible.\n\nLocations impacted include...\nVienna, Lake Of Egypt Area, Cypress, New Burnside, Buncombe, Belknap,\nand Simpson.\n\nThis includes Interstate 24 in Illinois between Mile Markers 6 and\n22.",
            "instruction": "If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.\n\nThis storm may intensify, so be certain to monitor local radio\nstations and available television stations for additional information\nand possible warnings from the National Weather Service.",

            "senderName": "NWS Jacksonville FL",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 25 at 9:38PM EDT until June 27 at 4:00AM EDT by NWS Jacksonville FL",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Georgia...\n\nSatilla River At Waycross affecting Pierce and Ware Counties.\n\nSatilla River At Atkinson affecting Brantley County.\n\nAdditional information is available at\nhttps://water.weather.gov/wfo/JAX\n\nThe next statement will be issued Friday evening at 945 PM EDT.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Satilla River at Waycross.\n\n* WHEN...Until late Friday night.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 16.0 feet, Flooding of agriculture and timberlands\nbegins. On the Ware County side, the Jamestown Road Boat Ramp is\nflooded. On the Pierce/Brantley county line at the State Road 121\nBridge the boat ramp and dirt access roads are flooded. At 17.0\nfeet, On the Ware County side, the Jamestown Road Boat Ramp parking\nlot and access road is flooded and Simmons Trail is flooded cutting\noff one residence. On the Pierce County side, the Okefenokee\nCountry Club Course Holes 14 through 16 begin to flood. At 18.0\nfeet, On the Pierce County side, the Okefenokee Country Club Golf\nCourse is generally closed. Riverwoods Drive low lying properties\nbegin to flood.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 9:30 PM EDT Thursday the stage was 17.1 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage early\nSaturday morning and continue falling to 14.5 feet Sunday\nevening.\n- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": null,
            "response": "Avoid",

            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 25 at 8:36PM CDT until June 29 at 3:25PM CDT by NWS Springfield MO",
            "description": "...The National Weather Service in Springfield MO has issued a Flood\nWarning for the following rivers in Missouri...\n\nLittle Osage River near Horton affecting Vernon County.\n\nFor the Little Osage River...including Horton...Minor flooding is\nforecast.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.\n\nThe next statement will be issued Friday evening at 845 PM CDT.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Little Osage River near Horton.\n\n* WHEN...From Saturday morning to Monday afternoon.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 45.0 feet, moderate flooding occurs at the gage site.\nLow lying areas along Route D near Stotesbury flood.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 7:45 PM CDT Thursday the stage was 32.1 feet.\n- Bankfull stage is 41.0 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage\nSaturday morning to a crest of 43.2 feet early Sunday\nmorning.             "senderName": "NWS Kansas City/Pleasant Hill MO",
            "headline": "Flash Flood Warning issued June 25 at 8:32PM CDT until June 25 at 10:30PM CDT by NWS Kansas City/Pleasant Hill MO",
            "description": "At 832 PM CDT, the public reported thunderstorms producing heavy rain\nacross the warned area. Between 3 and 4.5 inches of rain have fallen.\nFlash flooding is ongoing.\n\nHAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.\n\nSOURCE...Public reported.\n\nIMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,\nhighways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor\ndrainage and low-lying areas.\n\nSome locations that will experience flash flooding include...\nCreighton.",
            "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.",
            "response": "Avoid",

            "headline": "Flood Advisory issued June 25 at 8:31PM CDT until June 27 at 1:00PM CDT by NWS Tulsa OK",
            "description": "...The Flood Advisory is extended for the following rivers in\nOklahoma...\n\nIllinois River at Chewey affecting Delaware, Adair and Cherokee\nCounties.\n\nIllinois River near Tahlequah affecting Cherokee County.\n\nArkansas River near Muskogee affecting Muskogee County.\n\n...The Flood Advisory continues for the following rivers in\nOklahoma...\n\nBird Creek near Owasso-Mingo affecting Tulsa County.\n\n* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.\n\n* WHERE...Bird Creek near Owasso-Mingo.\n\n* WHEN...Until early Saturday afternoon.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 17.0 feet, faster flows are expected along the river\nbut no flooding occurs. Interests near the river and near Mohawk\nPark should continue to monitor later forecasts.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 7:00 PM CDT Thursday the stage was 12.8 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 17.0\nfeet early Saturday morning.\n- Action stage is 17.0 feet.\n- Flood stage is 18.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",

            "senderName": "NWS Tulsa OK",
            "headline": "Flood Advisory issued June 25 at 8:31PM CDT until June 28 at 1:00AM CDT by NWS Tulsa OK",
            "description": "...The Flood Advisory is extended for the following rivers in\nOklahoma...\n\nIllinois River at Chewey affecting Delaware, Adair and Cherokee\nCounties.\n\nIllinois River near Tahlequah affecting Cherokee County.\n\nArkansas River near Muskogee affecting Muskogee County.\n\n...The Flood Advisory continues for the following rivers in\nOklahoma...\n\nBird Creek near Owasso-Mingo affecting Tulsa County.\n\n* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.\n\n* WHERE...Arkansas River near Muskogee.\n\n* WHEN...Until early Sunday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 27.0 feet, no flooding occurs but low lying\nagricultural areas may be threatened. Continue to monitor later\nforecasts.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 8:00 PM CDT Thursday the stage was 26.7 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 27.1\nfeet Saturday morning.\n- Action stage is 27.0 feet.\n- Flood stage is 28.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": null,
            "response": "Avoid",
            "note": null,

            "senderName": "NWS Denver CO",
            "headline": "Special Weather Statement issued June 25 at 7:31PM MDT by NWS Denver CO",
            "description": "At 731 PM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking a line of outflow winds\nfrom strong thunderstorms extending from near Roggen to near Niwot,\nmoving south at 30 mph.\n\nHAZARD...Wind gusts of 50 to 55 mph.\n\nSOURCE...Radar indicated.\n\nIMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around\nunsecured objects.\n\nLocations impacted include...\nNortheastern Denver, northeastern Aurora, Thornton, eastern Arvada,\nWestminster, southern Longmont, Broomfield, Commerce City,\nNorthglenn, Brighton, Lafayette, Louisville, Erie, Federal Heights,\nFirestone, Denver International Airport, D.I.A Terminal and\nConcourses and Frederick.",
            "instruction": "Monitor the weather situation closely and be alert for threatening\nweather conditions.",

            "description": "...The Flood Advisory is extended for the following rivers in\nOklahoma...\n\nIllinois River at Chewey affecting Delaware, Adair and Cherokee\nCounties.\n\nIllinois River near Tahlequah affecting Cherokee County.\n\nArkansas River near Muskogee affecting Muskogee County.\n\n...The Flood Advisory continues for the following rivers in\nOklahoma...\n\nBird Creek near Owasso-Mingo affecting Tulsa County.\n\n* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.\n\n* WHERE...Illinois River at Chewey.\n\n* WHEN...Until Saturday evening.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 9.0 feet, no flooding occurs but all recreational\nfloating along the Illinois River ceases due to strong turbulence.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 7:15 PM CDT Thursday the stage was 6.1 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 9.0\nfeet Saturday morning.\n- Action stage is 9.0 feet.\n- Flood stage is 12.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",

            "headline": "Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued June 25 at 7:30PM MDT until June 25 at 8:15PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM",
            "description": "SVRABQ\n\nThe National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a\n\n* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...\nNortheastern Union County in northeastern New Mexico...\n\n* Until 815 PM MDT.\n\n* At 730 PM MDT, a severe thunderstorm was located 9 miles northwest\nof Seneca, or 19 miles north of Clayton, moving southeast at 15\nmph.\n\nHAZARD...Golf ball size hail and 60 mph wind gusts.\n\nSOURCE...Radar indicated.\n\nIMPACT...People and animals outdoors will be injured. Expect hail\ndamage to roofs, siding, windows, and vehicles. Expect\nwind damage to roofs, siding, and trees.\n\n* Locations impacted include...\nSeneca, Clayton Lake State Park and Moses.",
            "instruction": "Anyone outdoors should move to shelter inside a well-built structure\nand stay away from windows. This storm is capable of producing\ndangerous hail and damaging winds.",

            "senderName": "NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM",
            "headline": "Dust Advisory issued June 25 at 7:29PM MDT until June 25 at 8:15PM MDT by NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM",
            "description": "The National Weather Service in El Paso has issued a\n\n* Dust Advisory for...\nEl Paso County in western Texas...\n\n* Until 815 PM MDT.\n\n* At 727 PM MDT, a wall of dust was pushing across El Paso, moving\neast at 30 mph.\n\nHAZARD...Less than two miles visibility with strong wind in excess\nof 40 mph.\n\nSOURCE...Doppler radar.\n\nIMPACT...Hazardous travel.\n\nLocations impacted include...\nFar East El Paso, Mission Valley, Tornillo, Clint, Horizon City,\nFabens, Hueco Tanks, San Elizario, Indian Cliffs Ranch, Socorro,\nSparks, Homestead Meadows, Lake Way Estates, and Montana Vista.\n\nThe wind and dust will slowly weaken as they approach far east El\nPaso County and the Hueco Mountains.",
            "instruction": "Blowing dust brings reduced visibility, leading to dangerous driving\nconditions. If driving, avoid blowing dust if possible. If caught in\ndense blowing dust, pull off the road, turn off your lights and keep\nyour foot off the brake.",
            "response": "Execute",
            "note": null,

            "senderName": "NWS Springfield MO",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 25 at 8:28PM CDT until June 28 at 1:20AM CDT by NWS Springfield MO",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in\nMissouri...\n\nSac River near Caplinger Mills affecting Cedar County.\n\nFor the Sac River...including Caplinger Mills...Moderate flooding is\nforecast.\n\n* WHAT...Moderate flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Sac River near Caplinger Mills.\n\n* WHEN...From late tonight to early Sunday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 20.0 feet, flood waters affect low lying areas near\nthe river including farmland along Highway N and between Highway W\nand Caplinger Mills. Cedar Creek...a tributary of the Sac River\nbackwaters and floods portions of Highway 39 and south of Cedar\nSprings.\n\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 7:45 PM CDT Thursday the stage was 12.9 feet.\n- Bankfull stage is 16.0 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage\njust after midnight tonight to a crest of 21.4 feet early\nSaturday morning. It will then fall below flood stage\nSaturday evening.\n- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Many flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nBe especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the\ndangers of flooding.\n\nMotorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive\ncars through flooded areas.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.\n\nThe next statement will be issued Friday morning at 1100 AM CDT.",
            "response": "Avoid",
            "note": null,

            "senderName": "NWS Tallahassee FL",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 25 at 9:24PM EDT until June 28 at 11:00PM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...\n\nChoctawhatchee River near Bruce (SR 20) affecting Walton and\nWashington Counties.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and forecast to continue.\n\n* WHERE...Choctawhatchee River near Bruce (SR 20).\n\n* WHEN...Until late Sunday evening.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 14.0 feet, Big Cedar, Cowford, and Choctawhatchee\nRiver Roads begin to flood in Walton County. Flood waters impact\nstorage areas underneath homes on the west banks of the\nChoctawhatchee River. Low areas along Strickland Road in\nWashington County become subject to flooding.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 7:45 PM CDT Thursday the stage was 14.9 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours\nending at 7:45 PM CDT Thursday was 14.9 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage\nlate Sunday morning and continue falling to 12.8 feet Tuesday\nevening.\n- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.\n- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of\n14.9 feet on 02/28/2016.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive\ncars through flooded areas.\n\nCaution is urged when walking near riverbanks.\n\nBe especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the\ndangers of flooding.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.\n\nThe next statement will be issued by Friday afternoon at 430 PM CDT.",
            "response": "Avoid",
            "note": null,

            "headline": "Special Weather Statement issued June 25 at 7:21PM MDT by NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM",
            "description": "At 719 PM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm 7\nmiles southeast of Gage, moving northeast at 15 mph. Localized\ndownburst winds with this storm could produce blowing dust around\nInterstate 10. Other outflow boundaries and storms will continue to\ninteract over the next hour. Most storms will be short lived, but\nwill produce strong winds and blowing dust.\n\nHAZARD...Wind gusts up to 50 mph.\n\nSOURCE...Radar indicated.\n\nIMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around\nunsecured objects.\n\nLocations impacted include...\nDeming, Columbus, Gage, Akela, Carzalia Valley, Hermanas,\nand Sunshine.",
            "instruction": "If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.",

            "description": "...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in\nFlorida...Alabama...\n\nEscambia River Near Century affecting Escambia and Santa Rosa\nCounties.\n\nFor the Escambia River...including Century...Minor flooding is\nforecast.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Escambia River near Century.\n\n* WHEN...Until Sunday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 17.0 feet, considerable flooding of lowlands.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 8:00 PM CDT Thursday the stage was 17.9 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to remain near 17.9 feet through\njust after midnight tonight. It will then fall below flood stage\nearly Sunday morning.\n- Flood stage is 17.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov/mob.             "headline": "Special Weather Statement issued June 25 at 7:15PM MDT by NWS Denver CO",
            "description": "At 715 PM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm 9\nmiles north of Jackson Reservoir, or 25 miles northwest of Fort\nMorgan, moving southeast at 50 mph.\n\nHAZARD...Landspouts, wind gusts of 50 to 55 mph, and penny size hail.\n\nSOURCE...Radar indicated.\n\nIMPACT...Minor damage to outdoor objects is possible.             "instruction": "Monitor the weather situation closely and be alert for threatening\nweather conditions.\n\nHeavy rain is occurring with this storm and may lead to flooding.             "description": "...RED FLAG WARNING THIS EVENING FOR FIRE WEATHER ZONE 413 IS\nCANCELLED...\n\n...RED FLAG WARNING IN EFFECT FROM NOON FRIDAY TO MIDNIGHT MDT\nFRIDAY NIGHT FOR SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS FOR FIRE WEATHER ZONE\n422...\n\n* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zone 422 Sawtooth Range/Northern\nSawtooth NF.\n\n* IMPACTS...Critical fire weather conditions are expected.\nLightning may generate new fire starts. Any new fire starts or\nexisting fires may spread rapidly.\n\n* THUNDERSTORMS...A mix of wet and dry thunderstorms with 20 to\n35 percent coverage.\n\n* OUTFLOW WINDS...Gusts over 30 mph possible.",
            "instruction": "A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions\nare either occurring now, or will shortly based on these criteria\nfor Southeastern Idaho:\n\n- Relative humidity at or below 15 percent and wind gusts of at\nleast 25 mph in the mountains, or 30 mph in the Snake Plain.\n\n- Thunderstorm coverage of 25 percent, without specific rainfall\ncriteria.\n\n- Other high impact events deemed critical by the National\nWeather Service and area fire management agencies.",

            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 25 at 8:08PM CDT until June 26 at 12:15AM CDT by NWS Wichita KS",
            "description": "* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.\n\n* WHERE...A portion of southeast Kansas, including the following\ncounty, Neosho.\n\n* WHEN...Until 1215 AM CDT.\n\n* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying\nand flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 808 PM CDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges\nindicated heavy rain due to thunderstorms. Flooding is\nongoing or expected to begin shortly in the warned area.\nBetween 2 and 3 inches of rain have fallen.\n- Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are possible in the\nwarned area.\n- Some locations that will experience flooding include...\nChanute, Erie, St. Paul, Thayer, Galesburg, Earlton, Lake\nParsons, South Mound and Chanute Airport.",
            "instruction": "Do not drive into flooded areas or go around barricades. Nearly two\nfeet of water will carry most vehicles away. Turn around, don't\ndrown.\n\nPlease report observed flooding to local emergency services or law\nenforcement and request they pass this information to the National\nWeather Service when you can do so safely.",

            "description": "...The National Weather Service in Norman has issued a Flood\nAdvisory for the following rivers in Oklahoma...\n\nSalt Fork Arkansas River at Tonkawa affecting Noble, Kay and\nGrant Counties.\n\n* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.\n\n* WHERE...Salt Fork Arkansas River at Tonkawa.\n\n* WHEN...From this evening to Saturday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 15.0 feet, Within bank flows move along the river\nfrom eastern Grant County... across Kay County... to the\nconfluence with the Arkansas River below Ponca City.             "headline": "Special Weather Statement issued June 25 at 8:03PM CDT by NWS Springfield MO",
            "description": "At 802 PM CDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm near\nSt. Paul, moving east at 20 mph.\n\nHAZARD...Wind gusts up to 50 mph and penny size hail.\n\nSOURCE...Radar indicated.\n\nIMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around\nunsecured objects. Minor hail damage to vegetation is\npossible.\n\nLocations impacted include...\nColumbus, Girard, Cherokee, Weir, Scammon, Mccune, West Mineral,\nRoseland, Beulah, Greenbush, Carona, Skidmore, Brazilton, and\nStippville.",
            "instruction": "If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.\n\nTorrential rainfall is also occurring with this storm and may lead to\nlocalized flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded\nroadways.",

            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 25 at 8:03PM CDT until June 27 at 2:05PM CDT by NWS Wichita KS",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Kansas...\n\nVerdigris River at Altoona affecting Wilson County.\n\nVerdigris River at Coffeyville affecting Montgomery County.\n\nVerdigris River at Independence affecting Montgomery and Wilson\nCounties.\n\n* WHAT...Moderate flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Verdigris River at Altoona.\n\n* WHEN...From Friday morning to early Saturday afternoon.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 21.0 feet, Flood waters begin to threaten outlining\nfacilities of the city's water plant. Water Plant's clearwell may\nbecome flooded.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 7:45 PM CDT Thursday the stage was 6.7 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage\ntomorrow morning to a crest of 21.0 feet tomorrow evening. It\nwill then fall below flood stage early Saturday morning.\n- Flood stage is 19.0 feet.",
            "instruction": "Do not drive into flooded areas or go around barricades. Nearly two\nfeet of water will carry most vehicles away. Turn around, don't\ndrown.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.\n\nThe next statement will be issued Friday morning at 815 AM CDT.",

            "description": "...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in\nOklahoma...\n\nChikaskia River near Blackwell affecting Kay and Grant Counties.\n\n* WHAT...Moderate flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Chikaskia River near Blackwell.\n\n* WHEN...Until early Saturday afternoon.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 31.0 feet, Several city blocks in the northeast\nportions of Blackwell may be affected.  Streets closest to the\nriver may be nearly impassable... with depths approaching 2 feet.\nHighway 177 north of Blackwell is overtopped... and Hubbard Road\nsoutheast of Blackwell is closed.             "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Indianapolis IN",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 25 at 9:01PM EDT until June 26 at 10:08AM EDT by NWS Indianapolis IN",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Indiana...\nIllinois...\n\nWhite River at Petersburg.\n\nWabash River at Mount Carmel.\n\nWabash River at Vincennes.\n\n...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in\nIllinois...Indiana...\n\nWabash River at Riverton.\n\n...The Flood Warning is cancelled for the following rivers in\nIndiana...Illinois...\n\nWhite River at Hazleton.\n\nWabash River at Hutsonville Legacy Power Plant Site.\n\n.Minor flooding continues on the lower White River and the lower\nWabash. Additional rainfall over the next few days is expected to\nbring additional crests to the these rivers including spots that\nhave gone below flood and bring additional minor flooding or\nlengthen the amount of time above flood stage for the lower White\nand lower Wabash rivers.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring.\n\n* WHERE...Wabash River at Riverton.\n\n* WHEN...Until late tomorrow morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 16.0 feet, Some agricultural lands underwater.  A few\nrural roads in Crawford County, Illinois close as water backs up\nMinnow Slough.  High water affects campground at Leaverton Park in\nPalestine.  A few private roads near the Gill Township levee in\nSullivan County may flood.  Water level is at the top of most\nmakeshift levees.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 8:00 PM EDT Thursday /7:00 PM CDT Thursday/ the stage was\n15.4 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours\nending at 8:00 PM EDT Thursday /7:00 PM CDT Thursday/ was\n17.0 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage\nlate this evening and continue falling and remain below flood\nstage.\n- Flood stage is 15.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nBe especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the\ndangers of flooding.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov/ind.\n\nThe next statement should be issued this evening by around 1015 PM\nEDT /915 PM CDT/.",

            "event": "Flood Warning",
            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Indianapolis IN",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 25 at 9:01PM EDT until July 2 at 11:00AM EDT by NWS Indianapolis IN",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Indiana...\nIllinois...\n\nWhite River at Petersburg.\n\nWabash River at Mount Carmel.\n\nWabash River at Vincennes.\n\n...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in\nIllinois...Indiana...\n\nWabash River at Riverton.\n\n...The Flood Warning is cancelled for the following rivers in\nIndiana...Illinois...\n\nWhite River at Hazleton.\n\nWabash River at Hutsonville Legacy Power Plant Site.\n\n.Minor flooding continues on the lower White River and the lower\nWabash. Additional rainfall over the next few days is expected to\nbring additional crests to the these rivers including spots that\nhave gone below flood and bring additional minor flooding or\nlengthen the amount of time above flood stage for the lower White\nand lower Wabash rivers.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Wabash River at Mount Carmel.\n\n* WHEN...Until Thursday, July 02.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 21.0 feet, River Road in the Mount Carmel, Illinois\narea begins to flood.  Lowland flooding in progress.  A few local\nriver roads are closed by high water.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 7:45 PM EDT Thursday /6:45 PM CDT Thursday/ the stage was\n19.9 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours\nending at 7:45 PM EDT Thursday /6:45 PM CDT Thursday/ was\n20.0 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 20.7\nfeet Monday evening. It will then fall below flood stage late\nWednesday evening.\n- Flood stage is 19.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nBe especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the\ndangers of flooding.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov/ind.\n\nThe next statement should be issued this evening by around 1015 PM\nEDT /915 PM CDT/.",
            "response": "Avoid",
            "note": null,
            "parameters": {

                "FLSIND"
              ],

            "headline": "Flood Advisory issued June 25 at 7:59PM CDT until June 25 at 10:15PM CDT by NWS St Louis MO",
            "description": "* WHAT...Urban area and small stream flooding caused by excessive\nrainfall continues.\n\n* WHERE...Northern Franklin County in east central Missouri...\n\n* WHEN...Until 1015 PM CDT.\n\n* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.\nWater over roadways.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 758 PM CDT, Doppler radar indicated the heavy rain has ended\nfor the time being.  However, runoff from earlier rain continues\nand flooding is still a threat.             "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.",

            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 25 at 7:59PM CDT until June 27 at 10:47AM CDT by NWS Wichita KS",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in\nKansas...\n\nChikaskia River near Corbin affecting Sumner County.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Chikaskia River near Corbin.\n\n* WHEN...Until late Saturday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 13.0 feet, Left bank overflows extend out to about\n100 yards. A low water bridge on South Sumner Road, 3 miles\ndownstream from gage site or 2 miles southwest of Corbin, floods.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 7:30 PM CDT Thursday the stage was 14.2 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 15.0\nfeet just after midnight tonight. It will then fall below\nflood stage late tomorrow evening.\n- Flood stage is 10.0 feet.",
            "instruction": "Do not drive into flooded areas or go around barricades. Nearly two\nfeet of water will carry most vehicles away. Turn around, don't\ndrown.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.\n\nThe next statement will be issued Friday morning at 800 AM CDT.",

            "headline": "Special Weather Statement issued June 25 at 6:57PM MDT by NWS Glasgow MT",
            "description": "At 656 PM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm near\nJordan, moving northeast at 15 mph.\n\nHAZARD...Penny size hail.\n\nSOURCE...Radar indicated.\n\nIMPACT...Minor damage to outdoor objects is possible.\n\nLocations impacted include...\nJordan.",
            "instruction": "If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.\n\nTorrential rainfall is also occurring with this storm and may lead to\nlocalized flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded\nroadways.",

            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Tulsa OK",
            "headline": "Flood Watch issued June 25 at 7:57PM CDT until June 26 at 7:00AM CDT by NWS Tulsa OK",
            "description": "* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be\npossible.\n\n* WHERE...Portions of east central and northeast Oklahoma, including\nthe following counties, in east central Oklahoma, Cherokee,\nMuskogee and Okfuskee. In northeast Oklahoma, Adair, Craig, Creek,\nDelaware, Mayes, Northeast Osage, Nowata, Okmulgee, Ottawa,\nPawnee, Rogers, Southeast Osage, Tulsa, Wagoner, Washington OK and\nWestern Osage.\n\n* WHEN...Until 7 AM CDT Friday.\n\n* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,\ncreeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- An additional round of thunderstorms is expected to develop\nand move across northeast Oklahoma later tonight. Additional\nheavy rainfall is likely with widespread 1 to 2 inches and\nlocally 3+ inches possible by Friday morning. Already\nsaturated ground will create runoff that can lead to the\nrapid onset of flooding wherever thunderstorms occur. Swollen\nstreams and creeks will also be impacted by runoff caused by\nadditional heavy rainfall.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood\nWarnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared\nto take action should flooding develop.",
            "response": "Prepare",
            "note": null,

            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 25 at 7:53PM CDT by NWS Little Rock AR",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in\nArkansas...\n\nCache River Near Patterson affecting Woodruff and Jackson\nCounties.\n\nFor the Cache River...including Patterson...Minor flooding is\nforecast.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Cache River near Patterson.\n\n* WHEN...Until further notice.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 10.0 feet, Pastureland and cropland not protected by\nlevees in Jackson and Woodruff counties affected. Water is over\nportions of State Highway 37 and deep along the shoulders of State\nHighway 18 near Grubbs. Water over portions of Woodruff County\nRoad 775 north of State Highway 260.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 7:15 PM CDT Thursday the stage was 9.7 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to fall to 9.0 feet next\nTuesday.\n- Flood stage is 9.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive\ncars through flooded areas.\n\nRiver forecasts are based on current conditions and rainfall\nforecasted to occur over the next 24 hours. During periods of\nflooding...Evening forecasts are reissued with updated rainfall\nforecasts.\n\nObserved and forecasted stage data plots are available on our\nAdvanced Hydrologic Prediction Service web page at...\nwww.weather.gov/lzk\n\nUnder the Current Conditions section...Select River and Lakes AHPS.\n\nThe next statement will be issued Friday evening at 800 PM CDT.",
            "response": "Avoid",
            "note": null,

            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS New Orleans LA",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 25 at 7:53PM CDT until July 3 at 7:00PM CDT by NWS New Orleans LA",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in\nLouisiana...Mississippi...\n\nPearl River Near Bogalusa affecting Pearl River and Washington\nCounties.\n\nPearl River Near Pearl River affecting Pearl River, St. Tammany and\nHancock Counties.\n\nPascagoula River At Graham Ferry affecting Jackson County.\n\nFor the Lower Pearl River...including Bogalusa, Pearl River...Minor\nflooding is forecast.\nFor the Pascagoula River...including Graham Ferry...Minor flooding is\nforecast.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Pearl River near Pearl River.\n\n* WHEN...Until Friday, July 03.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 15.5 feet, Secondary roads to the river and throughout\nHoney Island Swamp are inundated. Property in the vicinity of the\ngage is flooded threatening about 20 homes along the left bank. The\nBogue Chitto National Wildlife Refuge will be closed to hunting at\nthe 15.5 foot stage.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 7:00 PM CDT Thursday the stage was 15.0 feet.\n- Bankfull stage is 12.0 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending\nat 7:00 PM CDT Thursday was 15.0 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 14.9 feet\nSaturday morning. It will then fall below flood stage Friday,\nJuly 03.\n- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.\n- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 15.0\nfeet on 01/08/1911.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars\nthrough flooded areas.\n\nCaution is urged when walking near riverbanks.\n\nPlease report observed flooding to local emergency services or law\nenforcement and request they pass this information to the National\nWeather Service when you can do so safely.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov/lix.  Click on\nthe Rivers and Lakes menu for forecasts and observations.\n\nThe next statement will be issued when updates are needed.",
            "response": "Avoid",
            "note": null,

            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS New Orleans LA",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 25 at 7:53PM CDT until July 3 at 5:30PM CDT by NWS New Orleans LA",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in\nLouisiana...Mississippi...\n\nPearl River Near Bogalusa affecting Pearl River and Washington\nCounties.\n\nPearl River Near Pearl River affecting Pearl River, St. Tammany and\nHancock Counties.\n\nPascagoula River At Graham Ferry affecting Jackson County.\n\nFor the Lower Pearl River...including Bogalusa, Pearl River...Minor\nflooding is forecast.\nFor the Pascagoula River...including Graham Ferry...Minor flooding is\nforecast.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Pearl River near Bogalusa.\n\n* WHEN...Until Friday, July 03.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 20.0 feet, Woodlands and crop acreage along the river\nwill be flooded. The Bogue Chitto Wildlife Management area will be\ninundated with water in recreational camps and over access roads.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 7:15 PM CDT Thursday the stage was 19.6 feet.\n- Bankfull stage is 15.0 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending\nat 7:15 PM CDT Thursday was 19.6 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 20.0 feet\nSunday morning. It will then fall below flood stage Friday, July\n03.\n- Flood stage is 18.0 feet.\n- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 20.0\nfeet on 02/14/2021.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars\nthrough flooded areas.\n\nCaution is urged when walking near riverbanks.\n\nPlease report observed flooding to local emergency services or law\nenforcement and request they pass this information to the National\nWeather Service when you can do so safely.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov/lix.  Click on\nthe Rivers and Lakes menu for forecasts and observations.\n\nThe next statement will be issued when updates are needed.",
            "response": "Avoid",
            "note": null,

            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in\nLouisiana...Mississippi...\n\nPearl River Near Bogalusa affecting Pearl River and Washington\nCounties.\n\nPearl River Near Pearl River affecting Pearl River, St. Tammany and\nHancock Counties.\n\nPascagoula River At Graham Ferry affecting Jackson County.\n\nFor the Lower Pearl River...including Bogalusa, Pearl River...Minor\nflooding is forecast.\nFor the Pascagoula River...including Graham Ferry...Minor flooding is\nforecast.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Pascagoula River at Graham Ferry.\n\n* WHEN...Until Monday afternoon.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 16.0 feet, River property at Cumbest Bluff will be cut\noff by high water and some river roads will be impassable.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 6:45 PM CDT Thursday the stage was 16.7 feet.\n- Bankfull stage is 15.0 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending\nat 6:45 PM CDT Thursday was 16.8 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 17.5 feet\ntomorrow morning.             "instruction": "Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars\nthrough flooded areas.\n\nCaution is urged when walking near riverbanks.\n\nPlease report observed flooding to local emergency services or law\nenforcement and request they pass this information to the National\nWeather Service when you can do so safely.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov/lix.             "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in\nMississippi...\n\nPearl River Near Monticello affecting Lawrence County.\n\nPearl River Near Rockport affecting Copiah and Simpson Counties.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Pearl River near Monticello.\n\n* WHEN...Until Sunday afternoon.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 7:15 PM CDT Thursday the stage was 23.3 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is cresting.\n- Flood stage is 22.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive\ncars through flooded areas.\n\nBe especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the\ndangers of flooding.\n\nTurn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.water.noaa.gov/wfo/jan\n\nThe next statement will be issued Friday morning at 700 AM CDT.",

            "headline": "Flood Advisory issued June 25 at 5:51PM MST until June 25 at 7:45PM MST by NWS Tucson AZ",
            "description": "* WHAT...Urban area and small stream flooding caused by excessive\nrainfall is expected.\n\n* WHERE...Eastern Pima County in southeastern Arizona...\n\n* WHEN...Until 745 PM MST.\n\n* IMPACTS...Rises in small streams and normally dry washes. Some\nlow-water crossings may become impassable.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 551 PM MST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to\nthunderstorms. This  will cause urban and small stream flooding.\nBetween 0.5 and 1 inch of rain has fallen.\n- Some locations that will experience flooding include...\nTucson and Rita Ranch.\n- This includes Interstate 10 between mile markers 272 and 277.\n\nThis includes the following Flash Flood Prone Locations...\nOld Spanish Trl at Rincon Creek, Camino Loma Alta at Rincon Creek\nand Old Spanish Trail at Jeremy Wash.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nIn hilly terrain there are hundreds of low water crossings which are\npotentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not attempt to cross flooded\nroads. Find an alternate route.",

            "description": "* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.\n\n* WHERE...Northeastern Bates County in west central Missouri...\nSoutheastern Cass County in west central Missouri...\nNorthwestern Henry County in west central Missouri...\nSouthwestern Johnson County in west central Missouri...\n\n* WHEN...Until 1030 PM CDT.\n\n* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 746 PM CDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to\nthunderstorms.             "instruction": "Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.",

            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 25 at 7:37PM CDT until June 27 at 12:00PM CDT by NWS Kansas City/Pleasant Hill MO",
            "description": "...The National Weather Service in Kansas City/Pleasant Hill has\nissued a Flood Warning for the following rivers in Missouri...\n\nPetite Saline Creek near Boonville affecting Cooper County.\n\n* WHAT...Moderate flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Petite Saline Creek near Boonville.\n\n* WHEN...Until Saturday afternoon.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 16.0 feet, Low lying woodlands and fields near the\ncreek flood. At 19.5 feet, The creek floods U Highway about 4 miles\nsoutheast of Boonville.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 6:30 PM CDT Thursday the stage was 14.0 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late\nthis evening to a crest of 21.0 feet early tomorrow afternoon. It\nwill then fall below flood stage early Saturday morning.\n- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nMotorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars\nthrough flooded areas.\n\nThis product along with additional weather and stream information is\navailable at www.weather.gov/kc/.",

            "senderName": "NWS Mobile AL",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 25 at 7:31PM CDT until June 30 at 8:00AM CDT by NWS Mobile AL",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in\nMississippi...\n\nChickasawhay At Leakesville affecting Greene and George Counties.\n\nFor the Chickasawhay River...including Waynesboro, Leakesville...\nMinor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Chickasawhay at Leakesville.\n\n* WHEN...Until Tuesday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 26.0 feet, flooding at the highway bridge begins.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 7:15 PM CDT Thursday the stage was 26.5 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage early\nTuesday morning and continue falling to 17.6 feet Tuesday\nevening.\n- Flood stage is 20.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov/mob. Click on\nthe Rivers and Lakes menu for forecasts and observations.\n\nThe next statement will be issued when updates occur.",
