            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 25 at 7:28PM CDT until June 30 at 6:00AM CDT by NWS Lake Charles LA",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in\nLouisiana...\n\nCalcasieu River Near Glenmora\n\nCalcasieu River near White Oak Park\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Calcasieu River near White Oak Park.\n\n* WHEN...Until Tuesday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 3.0 feet, Water over lowest portions of Goos Ferry\nRoad. Cars should be moved to higher ground.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 5:35 PM CDT Thursday the stage was 2.8 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours\nending at 5:35 PM CDT Thursday was 3.4 feet.\n- Forecast...The river will oscillate above flood stage with a\nmaximum value of 3.0 feet tomorrow morning. It will fall\nbelow flood stage early Tuesday morning.\n- Flood stage is 2.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",

            "senderName": "NWS Lake Charles LA",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 25 at 7:28PM CDT until June 30 at 1:00AM CDT by NWS Lake Charles LA",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in\nLouisiana...\n\nCalcasieu River Near Glenmora\n\nCalcasieu River near White Oak Park\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Calcasieu River near Glenmora.\n\n* WHEN...Until early Tuesday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 12.0 feet, When the river is rising and the gauge\nreading is forecast to reach 12 feet or higher. Roads upstream\nfrom Glenmora, including Strothers Crossing Road near the\ncommunity of Calcasieu and Price Crossing Road near Hineston have\nwater on them and are subject to being closed. Also, flooding of\nforested areas near the river will occur.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 6:45 PM CDT Thursday the stage was 13.1 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours\nending at 6:45 PM CDT Thursday was 13.5 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage\nMonday evening and continue falling to 11.7 feet Tuesday\nevening.\n- Flood stage is 12.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": null,
            "response": "Avoid",

            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 25 at 7:26PM CDT until June 27 at 8:23PM CDT by NWS Jackson MS",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in\nMississippi...\n\nBig Black River Near Bovina affecting Warren and Hinds Counties.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Big Black River near Bovina.\n\n* WHEN...Until Saturday evening.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 7:15 PM CDT Thursday the stage was 28.0 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 31.0\nfeet tomorrow morning.\n- Flood stage is 28.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive\ncars through flooded areas.\n\nBe especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the\ndangers of flooding.\n\nTurn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.water.noaa.gov/wfo/jan\n\nThe next statement will be issued Friday morning at 700 AM CDT.",

            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 25 at 7:24PM CDT until June 27 at 11:00AM CDT by NWS St Louis MO",
            "description": "...The National Weather Service in St Louis has issued a Flood\nWarning for the following rivers in Missouri...\n\nHinkson Creek at Columbia.\n\nRiver forecasts are based on observed precipitation and forecast\nprecipitation for the next 24 hours.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Hinkson Creek at Columbia.\n\n* WHEN...From this evening to Saturday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 17.7 feet, Height of the soccer practice field,\nprotected by a levee to about 25.5 feet.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 7:00 PM CDT Thursday the stage was 9.4 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late\nthis evening to a crest of 16.9 feet just after midnight tonight.\nIt will then fall below flood stage late tonight.\n- Flood stage is 15.0 feet.",
            "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads.             "event": "Flood Watch",
            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Kansas City/Pleasant Hill MO",
            "headline": "Flood Watch issued June 25 at 7:09PM CDT until June 26 at 7:00AM CDT by NWS Kansas City/Pleasant Hill MO",
            "description": "* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be\npossible.\n\n* WHERE...Portions of Kansas, including the following areas, Johnson\nKS, Leavenworth, Linn KS, Miami and Wyandotte and Missouri,\nincluding the following areas, Bates, Carroll, Cass, Chariton,\nClay, Cooper, Henry, Howard, Jackson, Johnson MO, Lafayette,\nPettis, Platte, Ray and Saline.\n\n* WHEN...Until 7 AM CDT Friday.\n\n* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,\ncreeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- Additional rounds of showers and thunderstorms are anticipated in\nthe area this evening and overnight and the environment remains\nfavorable for efficient rainfall.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood\nWarnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared\nto take action should flooding develop.",
            "response": "Prepare",
            "note": null,

            "description": "* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.\n\n* WHERE...Portions of northwest and western Oklahoma, including the\nfollowing counties, in northwest Oklahoma, Ellis and Woodward.             "headline": "Flash Flood Warning issued June 25 at 6:45PM CDT until June 25 at 9:45PM CDT by NWS Amarillo TX",
            "description": "FFWAMA\n\nThe National Weather Service in Amarillo has issued a\n\n* Flash Flood Warning for...\nSouthern Hemphill County in the panhandle of Texas...\n\n* Until 945 PM CDT.\n\n* At 645 PM CDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing\nheavy rain across the warned area. The expected rainfall rate is\n1.5 to 2 inches in 1 hour. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected\nto begin shortly.\n\nHAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.\n\nSOURCE...Radar.\n\nIMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban\nareas, highways, streets and underpasses as well as\nother poor drainage and low-lying areas.\n\n* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...\nLake Marvin.",
            "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nBe aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.\n\nStay away or be swept away. River banks and culverts can become\nunstable and unsafe.\n\nRemain alert for flooding even in locations not receiving rain.\nArroyos, streams, and rivers can become raging killer currents in a\nmatter of minutes, even from distant rainfall.",
            "response": "Avoid",
            "note": null,

            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 25 at 5:54PM CDT until June 26 at 6:00PM CDT by NWS Lake Charles LA",
            "description": "* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.\n\n* WHERE...A portion of central Louisiana, including the following\nparishes, Avoyelles, Evangeline and St. Landry.\n\n* WHEN...Until 600 PM CDT Friday.\n\n* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying\nand flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Numerous roads\nremain closed due to flooding. Streams continue to rise due to\nexcess runoff from earlier rainfall. Expect many areas of slow\nmoving or standing water. It will take several hours for all the\nwater from these storms to work through local drainage systems in\nurban areas.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 552 PM CDT, gauge reports runoff and standing water from\nprevious excessive rainfall. Flooding is already occurring in\nthe warned area.\n- Some locations that will experience flooding include...\nMelville, Palmetto, Morrow, Bayou Current, Port Barre,\nLebeau, Big Cane, Goudeau, Dupont and Whiteville.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nKeep children away from storm drains, culverts, creeks and streams.\n\nStay away or be swept away. River banks and culverts can become\nunstable and unsafe.",

            "senderName": "NWS Springfield MO",
            "headline": "Flash Flood Warning issued June 25 at 5:54PM CDT until June 26 at 12:00AM CDT by NWS Springfield MO",
            "description": "FFWSGF\n\nThe National Weather Service in Springfield has issued a\n\n* Flash Flood Warning for...\nNortheastern Barry County in southwestern Missouri...\nSouthwestern Christian County in southwestern Missouri...\nNorthern Stone County in southwestern Missouri...\n\n* Until midnight CDT tonight.\n\n* At 554 PM CDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated\nthunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between\n1 and 2.5 inches of rain have fallen. The expected rainfall rate\nis 1 to 3 inches in 1 hour. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected\nto begin shortly.\n\nHAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.\n\nSOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.\n\nIMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban\nareas, highways, streets and underpasses as well as\nother poor drainage and low-lying areas.\n\n* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...\nHighlandville, Crane, Galena, Mccord Bend, Hurley, Spokane, Elsey,\nPonce de Leon, Cape Fair, Wheelerville and Table Rock Lake.\n\nThis includes the following low water crossings...\nTin Can Hollow at Highway CC, Silver Lake Branch at Highway U, Dry\nCrane Creek at Jasmine Road, Tory Creek at Highway O, Little Crane\nCreek at Old Wire Road, Woods Fork at Woods Fork Road and Spring\nCreek at Highway CC.",
            "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Many flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nPlease report observed flooding to local emergency services or law\nenforcement and request they pass this information to the National\nWeather Service when you can do so safely.",
            "response": "Avoid",

            "headline": "Flash Flood Warning issued June 25 at 5:44PM CDT until June 25 at 11:15PM CDT by NWS Springfield MO",
            "description": "At 544 PM CDT, Emergency management reported flash flooding and\nwater rescues in Ash Grove and Ebenezer. Between 2 and 4.5 inches of\nrain have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 1 to 2 inches in 30\nminutes. Flash flooding is already occurring.\n\nHAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing\nflash flooding.\n\nSOURCE...Emergency management reported.\n\nIMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,\nurban areas, highways, low water crossings, streets and\nunderpasses.\n\nSome locations that will experience flash flooding include...\nNorthwestern Springfield, Bolivar, Buffalo, Greenfield, Willard,\nAsh Grove, Fair Grove, Walnut Grove, Pleasant Hope, Morrisville,\nEverton, Brookline, Dadeville, Halfway, Halltown, South\nGreenfield, Aldrich, Sacville, Cave Springs, Brighton, Eudora,\nEbenezer, Glidewell, Bois D'arc, Foose, Olive, March, Pennsboro\nand Stockton Lake.\n\nHighway CC is closed from Fair Grove to Highway 13 in northern\nGreene County.\n\nThis includes the following low water crossings...\nOpposum Creek at Bannon Road, Sac River at County Road 1247,\nTurkey Creek at Highway W, Slagle Creek at 86 Road, Sinking Creek\nat County Road 181, Clear Creek at Farm Road 87 and Asher Creek at\n560 Road.",
            "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Many flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nBe aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.\n\nPlease report observed flooding to local emergency services or law\nenforcement and request they pass this information to the National\nWeather Service when you can do so safely.",

            "senderName": "NWS Las Vegas NV",
            "headline": "Red Flag Warning issued June 25 at 3:41PM PDT until June 27 at 11:00PM PDT by NWS Las Vegas NV",
            "description": "...RED FLAG WARNING NOW IN EFFECT FOR STRONG WINDS AND LOW\nHUMIDITY FOR MUCH OF SOUTHEASTERN CALIFORNIA, SOUTHERN NEVADA,\nAND NORTHWESTERN ARIZONA FROM FRIDAY MORNING THROUGH SATURDAY\nEVENING...\n\n* TIMING...From Friday morning through Saturday evening.\n\n* WIND...Southwest winds 20 to 30 mph with gusts to 40 to 50\nmph.\n\n* HUMIDITY...5 to 15 percent.\n\n* IMPACTS...any fires that develop will likely spread rapidly.\nOutdoor burning is not recommended.",
            "instruction": "A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions\nare either occurring now...or will shortly. A combination of\nstrong winds...low relative humidity...and warm temperatures can\ncontribute to extreme fire behavior.",
            "response": "Prepare",

            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Salt Lake City UT",
            "headline": "Red Flag Warning issued June 25 at 4:39PM MDT until June 28 at 3:00AM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT",
            "description": "...THIS IS A PARTICULARLY DANGEROUS SITUATION FOR LOCATIONS\nINCLUDING MARYSVALE AND JUNCTION IN PIUTE COUNTY, PANGUITCH IN\nGARFIELD COUNTY, BEAVER AND MILFORD IN BEAVER COUNTY, CEDAR CITY\nAND ENOCH IN IRON COUNTY AND ENTERPRISE AND PINE VALLEY IN\nWASHINGTON COUNTY. THIS ALSO INCLUDES THE COTTONWOOD FIRE...\n\n* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zone 494 Henry Mountains and Fire\nWeather Zone 498 Grand Staircase.\n\n* WINDS...Southwest 20 to 30 mph with gusts up to 50 mph.\n\n* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...As low as 7 percent with little to no\novernight recovery Friday night.\n\n* IMPACTS...Critical fire weather conditions are expected. Any\nnew fire starts or existing fires may spread rapidly.",
            "instruction": "A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions\nare either occurring now...or are imminent. A combination of\nstrong winds...low relative humidity...and warm temperatures can\ncontribute to extreme fire behavior.",
            "response": "Prepare",
            "note": null,
            "parameters": {

            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Indianapolis IN",
            "headline": "Flood Watch issued June 25 at 6:38PM EDT until June 27 at 8:00AM EDT by NWS Indianapolis IN",
            "description": "* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be\npossible.\n\n* WHERE...Portions of south central, southwest, and west central\nIndiana, including the following counties, in south central\nIndiana, Lawrence and Monroe. In southwest Indiana, Daviess,\nGreene, Knox, Martin and Sullivan. In west central Indiana, Clay,\nOwen and Vigo.\n\n* WHEN...Through Saturday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,\ncreeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.\nLow-water crossings may be flooded.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- Multiple rounds of thunderstorms producing heavy rainfall\nwill impact southwest parts of central Indiana from this\nafternoon through early Saturday. 1 to 3 inches of rainfall\nis expected with locally higher amounts.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood\nWarnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared\nto take action should flooding develop.",

            "senderName": "NWS Springfield MO",
            "headline": "Flash Flood Warning issued June 25 at 5:31PM CDT until June 25 at 11:30PM CDT by NWS Springfield MO",
            "description": "FFWSGF\n\nThe National Weather Service in Springfield has issued a\n\n* Flash Flood Warning for...\nSoutheastern Barton County in southwestern Missouri...\nSouthern Cedar County in southwestern Missouri...\nNorthern Dade County in southwestern Missouri...\nWest Central Polk County in southwestern Missouri...\n\n* Until 1130 PM CDT.\n\n* At 531 PM CDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing\nheavy rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 3 inches of rain\nhave fallen. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin\nshortly.\n\nHAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.\n\nSOURCE...Radar.\n\nIMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban\nareas, highways, streets and underpasses as well as\nother poor drainage and low-lying areas.\n\n* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...\nStockton, Greenfield, Lockwood, Golden City, Fair Play, Jerico\nSprings, Arcola, Umber View Heights, Cane Hill, Neola, Wagoner,\nBona, Masters, Cedarville, Bearcreek, Arnica, Sylvania, Dunnegan,\nStockton Lake and Stockton State Park.",
            "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Many flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.",
            "response": "Avoid",

            "headline": "Hydrologic Outlook issued June 25 at 1:40PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK",
            "description": "ESFAFG\n\n...Locations Impacted...\nWhite Mountains, Fairbanks, Chatanika and Chena Basins, Parks Hwy\ncorridor from Fairbanks to Healy, Denali National Park\n\nA long-duration period of moderate rain is anticipated to start on\nSaturday evening and continue through Monday. This could impact a\nlarge portion of the Interior with a particular focus near Denali\nNational Park.\n\nReturn intervals indicate this as a 1 in 5 year to a 1 in 10 year\nevent.             "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 25 at 3:19PM CDT until June 28 at 7:00AM CDT by NWS Springfield MO",
            "description": "...The National Weather Service in Springfield MO has issued a Flood\nWarning for the following rivers in Kansas...\n\nSpring River above Baxter Springs affecting Cherokee County.\n\nFor the Spring River...including Baxter Springs...Minor flooding is\nforecast.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Spring River above Baxter Springs.\n\n* WHEN...From Friday morning to Sunday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 20.0 feet, Water level reaches the bottom of Rainbow\nBridge Crossing.\n\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 2:30 PM CDT Thursday the stage was 4.7 feet.\n- Bankfull stage is 12.0 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage\nlate tomorrow morning to a crest of 18.3 feet early Saturday\nmorning. It will then fall below flood stage early Sunday\nmorning.\n- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Many flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.\n\nThe next statement will be issued Friday morning at 1000 AM CDT.",

            "senderName": "NWS Wichita KS",
            "headline": "Flood Watch issued June 25 at 3:16PM CDT until June 26 at 7:00AM CDT by NWS Wichita KS",
            "description": "* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be\npossible.\n\n* WHERE...Portions of central, east central, south central, and\nsoutheast Kansas, including the following counties, in central\nKansas, Barton, Ellsworth, Lincoln, Marion, McPherson, Rice,\nRussell and Saline. In east central Kansas, Chase. In south\ncentral Kansas, Butler, Cowley, Harper, Harvey, Kingman, Reno,\nSedgwick and Sumner. In southeast Kansas, Allen, Chautauqua, Elk,\nGreenwood, Labette, Montgomery, Neosho, Wilson and Woodson.\n\n* WHEN...Through Friday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,\ncreeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.\nCreeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur\nin poor drainage and urban areas.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- Additional storms are expected to develop over southern\nKansas late this afternoon and evening. These storms will\nproduce high rainfall rates that may lead to flooding.",
            "instruction": "Do not drive into flooded areas or go around barricades. Nearly two\nfeet of water will carry most vehicles away. Turn around, don't\ndrown.\n\nBe aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.",
            "response": "Prepare",

            "headline": "Red Flag Warning issued June 25 at 1:03PM MST until June 28 at 8:00PM MST by NWS Tucson AZ",
            "description": "...RED FLAG WARNING IN EFFECT FROM 10 AM SATURDAY TO 8 PM MST\nSUNDAY FOR STRONG AND GUSTY WINDS, LOW RELATIVE HUMIDITY, AND\nHIGH FIRE DANGER FOR FIRE WEATHER ZONES 150, 151, 152, 153, AND\n154...\n\n* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zones 150, 151, 152, 153 and 154.\n\n* TIMING...From 10 AM Saturday to 8 PM MST Sunday.\n\n* WINDS...Southwest 15 to 25 mph with gusts 35 to 40 mph.\n\n* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...10 to 15 percent.\n\n* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop or are ongoing will have the\npotential to spread rapidly.",
            "instruction": "A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions\nare either occurring now...or are expected to develop. A\ncombination of strong winds...low relative humidity...and dry\nvegetation will create the potential for rapid and erratic fire\ngrowth.\n\nPlease advise the appropriate officials or fire crews in the\nfield of the Red Flag Warning for portions of Southeast Arizona.",

            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS San Diego CA",
            "headline": "Beach Hazards Statement issued June 25 at 1:02PM PDT until June 25 at 10:00PM PDT by NWS San Diego CA",
            "description": "* WHAT...Surf of 3 to 5 feet with sets to 6 feet on south-\nsouthwest facing beaches. Strong rip currents expected.\n\n* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County\nCoastal Areas.\n\n* WHEN...Through this evening.\n\n* IMPACTS...Hazardous swimming conditions. Localized minor tidal\noverflow possible this evening during high tide.",
            "instruction": "A beach hazards statement for elevated surf means that waves will\nbe high enough to cause danger to inexperienced swimmers in the\nwater. Elevated surf also frequently results in strong rip\ncurrents which can drag people away from the shore and possibly\nresult in drowning. Always swim near a lifeguard.",
            "response": "Avoid",
            "note": null,

            "senderName": "NWS Wichita KS",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 25 at 3:02PM CDT by NWS Wichita KS",
            "description": "...The National Weather Service in Wichita KS has issued a Flood\nWarning for the following rivers in Kansas...\n\nSalt Creek At Barnard affecting Lincoln County.\n\n* WHAT...Moderate flooding is forecast. This approaches the flood of\nrecord.\n\n* WHERE...Salt Creek at Barnard.\n\n* WHEN...From this evening until further notice.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 24.0 feet, Expect flooding of agricultural fields to\nan extent of 3/4 of a mile coverage. Flood waters cover Highway\n284 east of the creek bridge to around 260th Road, expect road\nclosure. Numerous roads along and near the Salt Creek flood.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 1:15 PM CDT Thursday the stage was 17.7 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage\nthis evening and continue rising to a crest of 24.1 feet\nearly tomorrow afternoon.\n- Flood stage is 21.0 feet.",
            "instruction": "Do not drive into flooded areas or go around barricades. Nearly two\nfeet of water will carry most vehicles away. Turn around, don't\ndrown.\n\nMotorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive\ncars through flooded areas.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.\n\nThe next statement will be issued late tonight at 315 AM CDT.",
            "response": "Avoid",
            "note": null,

            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 25 at 2:59PM CDT until June 27 at 9:08AM CDT by NWS Wichita KS",
            "description": "...Forecast flooding changed from Minor to Moderate severity and\nincreased in duration for the following rivers in Kansas...\n\nSlate Creek At Wellington affecting Sumner and Cowley Counties.\n\n* WHAT...Moderate flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Slate Creek at Wellington.\n\n* WHEN...From this evening to late Saturday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 23.5 feet, Expect extensive cropland and field\nflooding along the creek.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 2:00 PM CDT Thursday the stage was 16.8 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage\nthis evening to a crest of 22.0 feet tomorrow morning. It\nwill then fall below flood stage late tomorrow evening.\n- Flood stage is 19.0 feet.",
            "instruction": "Do not drive into flooded areas or go around barricades. Nearly two\nfeet of water will carry most vehicles away.             "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Amarillo TX",
            "headline": "Flood Watch issued June 25 at 2:58PM CDT until June 26 at 1:00AM CDT by NWS Amarillo TX",
            "description": "* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be\npossible.\n\n* WHERE...Portions of the Panhandle of Oklahoma, including the\nfollowing county, Beaver and the Panhandle of Texas, including the\nfollowing county, Lipscomb.\n\n* WHEN...Until 1 AM CDT Friday.\n\n* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,\ncreeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- Recent rainfall amounts of 3 to 6 inches may lead to\nexcessive runoff with any additional thunderstorms.\ntomorrow night.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood\nWarnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared\nto take action should flooding develop.",

            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Tucson AZ",
            "headline": "Extreme Heat Warning issued June 25 at 12:58PM MST until June 25 at 8:00PM MST by NWS Tucson AZ",
            "description": "* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions with afternoon temperatures of\n106 to 109 degrees. Localized Major Heat Risk.\n\n* WHERE...Southeast Pinal County, Tucson Metro Area, Upper Gila River\nValley, and Upper San Pedro River Valley (mainly north of Benson).\n\n* WHEN...Until 8 PM MST this evening.\n\n* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during\nextreme heat events.",
            "instruction": "To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and\nHealth Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in\nshaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat\nshould be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an\nemergency! Call 9 1 1.\n\nTake extra precautions if you work or spend time outside. When\npossible, reschedule strenuous activities to early morning or\nevening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat\nstroke. Wear lightweight and loose fitting clothing when possible and\ndrink plenty of water.",
            "response": "Execute",
            "note": null,

            "senderName": "NWS Wichita KS",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 25 at 2:56PM CDT until June 27 at 8:15PM CDT by NWS Wichita KS",
            "description": "...The National Weather Service in Wichita KS has issued a Flood\nWarning for the following rivers in Kansas...\n\nWhitewater River at Towanda affecting Butler County.\n\nWhitewater River at Augusta affecting Butler and Cowley Counties.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Whitewater River at Towanda.\n\n* WHEN...From Friday morning to Saturday evening.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 25.0 feet, Flooding over cropland becomes more\nwidespread. County roads flood at Southwest 40th Street on low\nspots near the river about 2 miles downstream of gage and along\nSouthwest 60th Street just west of Fulton Road near the river\nlocated 4 miles south of Towanda. Further downstream, 5 miles\nsouth of Towanda, expect flooding across Southwest 70th Street\nnear the river.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 2:30 PM CDT Thursday the stage was 2.4 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage\ntomorrow morning to a crest of 24.5 feet tomorrow evening. It\nwill then fall below flood stage Saturday morning.\n- Flood stage is 22.0 feet.",
            "instruction": "Do not drive into flooded areas or go around barricades. Nearly two\nfeet of water will carry most vehicles away. Turn around, don't\ndrown.\n\nMotorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive\ncars through flooded areas.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.\n\nThe next statement will be issued late tonight at 300 AM CDT.",
            "response": "Avoid",
            "note": null,

            "senderName": "NWS St Louis MO",
            "headline": "Flood Watch issued June 25 at 2:55PM CDT until June 26 at 7:00PM CDT by NWS St Louis MO",
            "description": "* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be\npossible.\n\n* WHERE...Portions of Illinois, including the following areas, Bond\nIL, Calhoun IL, Clinton IL, Fayette IL, Greene IL, Jersey IL,\nMacoupin IL, Madison IL, Marion IL, Monroe IL, Montgomery IL, Pike\nIL, Randolph IL, Saint Clair IL and Washington IL and Missouri,\nincluding the following areas, Audrain MO, Boone MO, Callaway MO,\nCole MO, Crawford MO, Franklin MO, Gasconade MO, Iron MO, Jefferson\nMO, Lincoln MO, Madison MO, Moniteau MO, Montgomery MO, Osage MO,\nPike MO, Reynolds MO, Saint Charles MO, Saint Francois MO, Saint\nLouis City MO, Saint Louis MO, Sainte Genevieve MO, Warren MO and\nWashington MO.\n\n* WHEN...Through Friday evening.\n\n* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,\ncreeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- Multiple waves of thunderstorms capable of heavy rainfall.\n- Some locations that may experience flooding include...\nSt. Louis, Columbia, O'Fallon, St. Charles, St. Peters,\nFlorissant, Chesterfield, Belleville, Jefferson City, Wildwood,\nUniversity City, Ballwin, Granite City, Wentzville, Alton,\nKirkwood, Maryland Heights, East St. Louis and Hazelwood.",
            "instruction": "You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action\nshould Flash Flood Warnings be issued.",
            "response": "Prepare",
            "note": null,

            "description": "* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be\npossible.\n\n* WHERE...Portions of Indiana, including the following areas, Clark\nIN, Crawford, Dubois, Floyd, Harrison IN, Orange, Perry and\nWashington IN and north central Kentucky, including the following\narea, Jefferson.\n\n* WHEN...Through Saturday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,\ncreeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.\nFlooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.             "description": "...The National Weather Service in Wichita KS has issued a Flood\nWarning for the following rivers in Kansas...\n\nWalnut River at Winfield affecting Butler and Cowley Counties.\n\nWalnut River at Augusta affecting Butler and Cowley Counties.\n\nWalnut River at Arkansas City affecting Cowley County.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Walnut River at Arkansas City.\n\n* WHEN...From Friday morning to Monday afternoon.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 20.0 feet, Considerable flooding of farmland is\nexpected. Widespread flooding of the park just upstream of the\ngage site is anticipated. East Chestnut Avenue east of By-pass is\nclosed due to water over roadway. Greens Farm Road floods between\nHighway 166 north to Dunbar Hill.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 2:15 PM CDT Thursday the stage was 9.6 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage\ntomorrow morning to a crest of 20.5 feet Saturday evening. It\nwill then fall below flood stage early Monday morning.\n- Flood stage is 18.0 feet.",
            "instruction": "Do not drive into flooded areas or go around barricades. Nearly two\nfeet of water will carry most vehicles away.             "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 25 at 2:49PM CDT until June 28 at 12:00AM CDT by NWS Wichita KS",
            "description": "...The National Weather Service in Wichita KS has issued a Flood\nWarning for the following rivers in Kansas...\n\nArkansas River at Arkansas City affecting Cowley County.\n\nArkansas River near Mulvane affecting Sumner and Sedgwick\nCounties.\n\nArkansas River at Oxford affecting Sumner County.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Arkansas River at Oxford.\n\n* WHEN...From Friday morning to early Sunday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 18.0 feet, Low lying agricultural fields flood north\nof the river gage site.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 1:45 PM CDT Thursday the stage was 11.9 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage\ntomorrow morning to a crest of 19.5 feet early tomorrow\nafternoon. It will then fall below flood stage early Saturday\nafternoon.\n- Flood stage is 17.0 feet.",
            "instruction": "Do not drive into flooded areas or go around barricades. Nearly two\nfeet of water will carry most vehicles away. Turn around, don't\ndrown.\n\nMotorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive\ncars through flooded areas.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.\n\nThe next statement will be issued late tonight at 300 AM CDT.",

            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Springfield MO",
            "headline": "Flood Watch issued June 25 at 2:46PM CDT until June 26 at 7:00PM CDT by NWS Springfield MO",
            "description": "* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be\npossible.\n\n* WHERE...Portions of southeast Kansas, including the following\nareas, Bourbon, Cherokee and Crawford and Missouri, including the\nfollowing areas, Barry, Barton, Benton, Camden, Cedar, Christian,\nDade, Dallas, Dent, Douglas, Greene, Hickory, Howell, Jasper,\nLaclede, Lawrence, Maries, McDonald, Miller, Morgan, Newton,\nOregon, Ozark, Phelps, Polk, Pulaski, Shannon, St. Clair, Stone,\nTaney, Texas, Vernon, Webster and Wright.\n\n* WHEN...Through Friday evening.\n\n* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,\ncreeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.\nFlooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water\ncrossings may be flooded.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- Multiple rounds of showers and thunderstorms will move\nthrough the area and bring 2 to 4 inches of rain with\nlocalized amounts up to 7 inches.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood\nWarnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared\nto take action should flooding develop.",
            "response": "Prepare",
            "note": null,

            "senderName": "NWS Wichita KS",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 25 at 2:45PM CDT until June 30 at 2:22AM CDT by NWS Wichita KS",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Kansas...\n\nNeosho River near Erie affecting Neosho County.\n\nNeosho River near Parsons affecting Neosho and Labette Counties.\n\nNeosho River near Chanute affecting Allen and Neosho Counties.\n\nNeosho River at Oswego affecting Cherokee and Labette Counties.\n\n* WHAT...Moderate flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Neosho River at Oswego.\n\n* WHEN...From Friday evening to early Tuesday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 22.5 feet, Riverside Park Drive floods from east of\nXavier Road, just south of the river gage bridge, to 100 yards\neast towards the water plant.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 7:00 AM CDT Thursday the stage was 8.6 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage\ntomorrow evening to a crest of 22.4 feet early Saturday\nafternoon. It will then fall below flood stage Monday\nmorning.\n- Flood stage is 17.0 feet.",
            "instruction": "Do not drive into flooded areas or go around barricades. Nearly two\nfeet of water will carry most vehicles away. Turn around, don't\ndrown.\n\nMotorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive\ncars through flooded areas.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.\n\nThe next statement will be issued late tonight at 245 AM CDT.",
            "response": "Avoid",

            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Wichita KS",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 25 at 2:45PM CDT until June 28 at 8:02AM CDT by NWS Wichita KS",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Kansas...\n\nNeosho River near Erie affecting Neosho County.\n\nNeosho River near Parsons affecting Neosho and Labette Counties.\n\nNeosho River near Chanute affecting Allen and Neosho Counties.\n\nNeosho River at Oswego affecting Cherokee and Labette Counties.\n\n* WHAT...Moderate flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Neosho River near Erie.\n\n* WHEN...From Friday morning to Sunday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 33.0 feet, The road 7 miles northwest of Erie at\n190th Road just west of Big Creek becomes flooded.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 2:15 PM CDT Thursday the stage was 12.9 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage\nlate tomorrow morning to a crest of 33.6 feet early tomorrow\nafternoon. It will then fall below flood stage Saturday\nevening.\n- Flood stage is 29.0 feet.",
            "instruction": "Do not drive into flooded areas or go around barricades. Nearly two\nfeet of water will carry most vehicles away. Turn around, don't\ndrown.\n\nMotorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive\ncars through flooded areas.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.\n\nThe next statement will be issued late tonight at 245 AM CDT.",
            "response": "Avoid",
            "note": null,

            "event": "Fire Weather Watch",
            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Albuquerque NM",
            "headline": "Fire Weather Watch issued June 25 at 1:43PM MDT until June 27 at 8:00PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM",
            "description": "...FIRE WEATHER WATCH REMAINS IN EFFECT FROM LATE SATURDAY MORNING\nTHROUGH SATURDAY EVENING DUE TO STRONG WINDS AND LOW RELATIVE\nHUMIDITY FOR MUCH OF NORTHWEST AND NORTHEAST NEW MEXICO AS WELL AS\nTHE CENTRAL HIGHLANDS...\n\n.Critical fire weather conditions will return on Saturday across much\nof northwest and northeast New Mexico as well as the Central\nHighlands. Strong southwest winds with gusts up to 45 mph and\nhumidity values falling below 15 percent are expected. Spotty wetting\nrainfall the next couple of days will not significantly improve fuel\ndryness, with the northwest remaining the driest portion of the\nstate. Any lightning-started fires will have the potential to grow\nquickly under these fire weather conditions.\n\n* AFFECTED AREA...Northwest Plateau (Zone 101), Northeast Plains\n(Zone 104), West Central Mountains (Zone 105), North Central\nMountains (Zone 120), Upper Rio Grande Valley and Lower Chama River\nValley (Zone 121), Northeast Highlands (Zone 123), and Central\nHighlands (Zone 125).\n\n* TIMING...From Saturday morning through Saturday evening.\n\n* 20 FOOT WINDS...Southwest winds 20 to 30 mph with gusts up to 45\nmph.\n\n* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Relative humidity between 8 to 15 percent.\n\n* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will spread rapidly. Outdoor\nburning is not recommended.",
            "instruction": "Please advise the appropriate officials or fire crews in the field of\nthis Fire Weather Watch.",
            "response": "Prepare",
            "note": null,
            "parameters": {

                "RFWABQ"
              ],

            "event": "Extreme Heat Warning",
            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Phoenix AZ",
            "headline": "Extreme Heat Warning issued June 25 at 12:35PM MST until June 25 at 8:00PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ",
            "description": "* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions. Afternoon temperatures 108 to\n112 degrees. Major Heat Risk.\n\n* WHERE...The entire Phoenix metropolitan area.\n\n* WHEN...Until 8 PM MST this evening.\n\n* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during\nextreme heat events. Overexposure can cause heat cramps and heat\nexhaustion to develop and, without intervention, can lead to heat\nstroke.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...In Maricopa County, call 2-1-1 to find a free\ncooling center, transportation, water, and more.\nhttp://www.maricopa.gov/heat",
            "instruction": "An Extreme Heat Warning means that a period of very hot temperatures,\neven by local standards, will occur. Actions should be taken to\nlessen the impact of the extreme heat.\n\nTake extra precautions if you work or spend time outside. When\npossible, reschedule strenuous activities to early morning or\nevening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat\nstroke. Wear lightweight and loose-fitting clothing when possible and\ndrink plenty of water.\n\nTo reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and\nHealth Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in\nshaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat\nshould be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an\nemergency! Call 9 1 1.\n\nPublic cooling shelters are available in some areas. Consult county\nofficials for more details.",
            "response": "Execute",
            "note": null,

            "senderName": "NWS Phoenix AZ",
            "headline": "Extreme Heat Warning issued June 25 at 12:35PM MST until June 25 at 8:00PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ",
            "description": "* WHAT...For the Extreme Heat Warning, dangerously hot conditions.\nAfternoon temperatures 108 to 115 degrees. Major Heat Risk.  For\nthe Wind Advisory, west winds 20 to 30 mph with gusts up to 50 mph.\n\n* WHERE...Imperial Valley including the city of El Centro.\n\n* WHEN...For the Extreme Heat Warning, until 8 PM PDT this evening.\nFor the Wind Advisory, from 11 AM to 11 PM PDT Saturday.\n\n* IMPACTS...Difficult driving conditions, especially for larger\nvehicles traveling along roads with crosswinds. Light, unsecured\nobjects may become airborne. Heat related illnesses increase\nsignificantly during extreme heat events.",
            "instruction": "A Wind Advisory means that sustained wind speeds of between 30 and 40\nmph are expected, or wind gusts of between 40 and 58 mph. Winds this\nstrong can make driving difficult, especially for high profile\nvehicles.\n\nIn addition, strong winds over desert areas could result in briefly\nlowered visibilities to well under a mile at times in blowing dust or\nblowing sand. Use extra caution.\n\nAn Extreme Heat Warning means that a period of very hot temperatures,\neven by local standards, will occur. Actions should be taken to\nlessen the impact of the extreme heat.\n\nTake extra precautions if you work or spend time outside. When\npossible, reschedule strenuous activities to early morning or\nevening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat\nstroke. Wear lightweight and loose-fitting clothing when possible and\ndrink plenty of water.\n\nTo reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and\nHealth Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in\nshaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat\nshould be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an\nemergency! Call 9 1 1.\n\nPublic cooling shelters are available in some areas. Consult county\nofficials for more details.",
            "response": "Execute",
            "note": null,

            "senderName": "NWS Phoenix AZ",
            "headline": "Extreme Heat Warning issued June 25 at 12:35PM MST until June 25 at 8:00PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ",
            "description": "* WHAT...For the Extreme Heat Warning, dangerously hot conditions.\nAfternoon temperatures 102 to 110 degrees. Major Heat Risk. For the\nWind Advisory, west winds 25 to 35 mph with gusts up to 55 mph.\n\n* WHERE...Imperial County Southwest.\n\n* WHEN...For the Extreme Heat Warning, until 8 PM PDT this evening.\nFor the Wind Advisory, from 5 PM Friday to 11 AM PDT Sunday.\n\n* IMPACTS...Difficult driving conditions, especially for larger\nvehicles traveling along roads with crosswinds. Light, unsecured\nobjects may become airborne. Heat related illnesses increase\nsignificantly during extreme heat events.",
            "instruction": "A Wind Advisory means that sustained wind speeds of between 30 and 40\nmph are expected, or wind gusts of between 40 and 58 mph. Winds this\nstrong can make driving difficult, especially for high profile\nvehicles.\n\nAn Extreme Heat Warning means that a period of very hot temperatures,\neven by local standards, will occur. Actions should be taken to\nlessen the impact of the extreme heat.\n\nTake extra precautions if you work or spend time outside. When\npossible, reschedule strenuous activities to early morning or\nevening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat\nstroke. Wear lightweight and loose-fitting clothing when possible and\ndrink plenty of water.\n\nTo reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and\nHealth Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in\nshaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat\nshould be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an\nemergency! Call 9 1 1.\n\nPublic cooling shelters are available in some areas. Consult county\nofficials for more details.",
            "response": "Execute",
            "note": null,

            "senderName": "NWS Norman OK",
            "headline": "Flood Watch issued June 25 at 2:21PM CDT until June 26 at 7:00AM CDT by NWS Norman OK",
            "description": "* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be\npossible.\n\n* WHERE...Portions of central, northern, and northwest Oklahoma,\nincluding the following counties, in central Oklahoma, Lincoln,\nLogan and Payne. In northern Oklahoma, Garfield, Grant, Kay and\nNoble. In northwest Oklahoma, Alfalfa, Ellis, Harper, Major, Woods\nand Woodward.\n\n* WHEN...Through Friday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,\ncreeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.\nCreeks and streams may rise out of their banks.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- Additional rounds of thunderstorms is expected this\nafternoon, evening, and tonight across the watch area with\nvery heavy rain possible.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood\nWarnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared\nto take action should flooding develop.",

            "headline": "Red Flag Warning issued June 25 at 12:10PM PDT until June 25 at 9:00PM PDT by NWS Spokane WA",
            "description": "...WARM, WINDY AND DRY THURSDAY...\n\n* Affected Area: Colville Reservation (Zone 702), Okanogan\nValley (Zone 703), Foothills of Central Washington Cascades\n(Zone 705), Waterville Plateau (Zone 706), Western Columbia\nBasin (Zone 707), Eastern Columbia Basin  -Palouse  -Spokane\nArea (Zone 708) and Lower Palouse  -Snake River (Zone 709).\n\n* Winds: Southwest 10 to 20 mph with gusts up to 30 mph.\n\n* Relative Humidities: 13 to 21 percent.\n\n* Impacts: Rapid fire spread is likely with any new or ongoing\nfires.",
            "instruction": "A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions\nare either occurring now....or will shortly. A combination of\nstrong winds...low relative humidity...and warm temperatures can\ncontribute to extreme fire behavior.",

            "senderName": "NWS Denver CO",
            "headline": "Fire Weather Watch issued June 25 at 1:09PM MDT until June 28 at 12:00AM MDT by NWS Denver CO",
            "description": "...PROLONGED CRITICAL FIRE WEATHER CONDITIONS EXPECTED FOR THE\nHIGH COUNTRY...\n\nA warm and dry airmass will coincide with considerably stronger\nwest and southwest winds this weekend, potentially continuing\ninto early next week. Sustained winds are expected to exceed\n20 to 30 mph across much of the high country beginning Saturday,\nwith gusts of 40 to 50 mph, strongest for exposed areas and\nhigher elevations. These conditions will drive very high fire\ndanger across the warned area, that may extend through the\nevening hours of Saturday driven by the enhanced winds. Any new\nstarts or established fires will likely spread rapidly under\nthese conditions.\n\n* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zones 211, 212, 213, 214, 217 and\n218.\n\n* TIMING...From Saturday morning through Saturday evening.\n\n* WINDS...Southwest 20 to 30 mph with gusts up to 50 mph.\n\n* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...11 to 15 percent.\n\n* IMPACTS...Conditions will be favorable for rapid fire spread.\nAvoid outdoor burning and any activity that may produce a\nspark and start a wildfire.",
            "instruction": "A Fire Weather Watch means that critical fire weather conditions\nare forecast to occur. Listen for later forecasts and possible\nRed Flag Warnings.",
            "response": "Prepare",
            "note": null,
            "parameters": {

            "senderName": "NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM",
            "headline": "Fire Weather Watch issued June 25 at 12:57PM MDT until June 28 at 8:00PM MDT by NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM",
            "description": "...CRITICAL FIRE WEATHER CONDITIONS POSSIBLE FOR SATURDAY-SUNDAY...\n\n.A strong upper-level trough from the Pacific Northwest will bring\nbreezy southwest winds for Gila National Forest and the Southwest\nNew Mexico Deserts on Saturday and Sunday. These winds will range\nfrom 15-25 mph. Combined with Min RH values in the mid-to-upper\nteens, gusts up to 40 mph, and insufficient fuel recovery from\nisolated showers and thunderstorms this weekend, these winds will\nraise fire weather conditions to near critical.\n\n* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zone 110 Southwest Mountains/Gila\nNF/Apache NF/GLZ and Fire Weather Zone 111 Southwest Deserts\nand Lowlands/Las Cruces BLM/GLZ.\n\n* TIMING...Saturday morning through Sunday evening.\n\n* WINDS...Southwest 15 to 25 mph with gusts up to 40 mph.\n\n* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...As low as 11 percent.\n\n* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will likely spread rapidly.\nOutdoor burning is not recommended.",
            "instruction": "A Fire Weather Watch means that critical fire weather conditions\nare forecast to occur. Listen for later forecasts and possible\nRed Flag Warnings.",

            "description": "* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be\npossible.\n\n* WHERE...Portions of central, east central, and west central\nIllinois, including the following counties, in central Illinois,\nMacon and Sangamon. In east central Illinois, Douglas and Edgar.\nIn west central Illinois, Morgan and Scott.\n\n* WHEN...Through Saturday afternoon.\n\n* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,\ncreeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- Between 1.5 and 3 inches of rain is likely with locally\nhigher amounts from late this afternoon through midday\nSaturday with the heaviest amounts late tonight and Friday.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood\nWarnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared\nto take action should flooding develop.",

            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 25 at 11:55AM PDT until June 27 at 12:56PM PDT by NWS Spokane WA",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in\nWashington...\n\nStehekin River at Stehekin affecting Chelan County.\n\nFor the Stehekin River...including Stehekin...Minor flooding is\nforecast.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and forecast to continue.\n\n* WHERE...Stehekin River at Stehekin.\n\n* WHEN...Until early Saturday afternoon.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 20.5 feet, water inundates some properties and\novertops the temporary corduroy bridge. Company Creek Road\ninundated at northern end. Battalion Creek culverts are beginning\nto be overtopped. Water begins damaging Wood Road.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 10:30 AM PDT Thursday the stage was 20.7 feet.\n- Bankfull stage is 19.5 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours\nending at 10:30 AM PDT Thursday was 21.0 feet.\n- Forecast...The river will remain between 20.6 and 20.8 feet\nthrough Thursday night, then will begin falling Friday\nmorning, dropping below flood stage this weekend.\n- Flood stage is 20.5 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive\ncars through flooded areas.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.\n\nThe next statement will be issued Friday afternoon at 1215 PM PDT.",

            "event": "Red Flag Warning",
            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Boise ID",
            "headline": "Red Flag Warning issued June 25 at 12:53PM MDT until June 27 at 6:00AM MDT by NWS Boise ID",
            "description": "...SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS FRIDAY AFTERNOON INTO SATURDAY...\n\n.A strong low pressure system will begin to move into the area\nlater today, bringing a cold front through the area early Friday\nmorning. Widespread showers will follow behind the front\nthroughout the day Friday into Saturday, however clearing behind\nthe front late Friday morning will enable scattered\nthunderstorm development. Thunderstorms may produce erratic\noutflow gusts up to 50 mph.\n\nThe National Weather Service in Boise has issued a Red Flag\nWarning for lightning, which is in effect from noon MDT /11 AM\nPDT/ Friday to 6 AM MDT /5 AM PDT/ Saturday. The Fire Weather\nWatch is no longer in effect.\n\n* AFFECTED AREA...In Idaho, Fire Weather Zones 400 Northern\nBoise BLM, 420 Treasure Valley BLM, 423 Owyhee Mountains, 424\nWestern Twin Falls BLM and 426 Southern Highlands. In Oregon,\nFire Weather Zones 670 Burns BLM, 671 Steens Mountain, 672\nSouthern Grasslands, 673 Central Canyonlands and 674\nNorthwestern Vale BLM.\n\n* TIMING...From noon MDT /11 AM PDT/ Friday to 6 AM MDT /5 AM\nPDT/ Saturday.\n\n* THUNDERSTORMS...Scattered coverage with abundant lightning.\n\n* OUTFLOW WINDS...Gusty erratic winds up to 50 mph.\n\n* IMPACTS...Any fire that develops will catch and spread\nquickly. Outdoor burning is not recommended.",
            "instruction": "A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions\nare either occurring now, or will occur shortly.",
            "response": "Prepare",
            "note": null,
            "parameters": {
              "AWIPSidentifier": [
                "RFWBOI"
              ],
              "WMOidentifier": [
                "WWUS85 KBOI 251853"
              ],
              "NWSheadline": [
                "RED FLAG WARNING IN EFFECT FROM NOON MDT /11 AM PDT/ FRIDAY TO 6 AM MDT /5 AM PDT/ SATURDAY FOR LIGHTNING FOR NORTHERN BOISE BLM...TREASURE VALLEY BLM...OWYHEE MOUNTAINS...WESTERN TWIN FALLS BLM...SOUTHERN HIGHLANDS...BURNS BLM...STEENS MOUNTAIN...SOUTHERN GRASSLANDS...CENTRAL CANYONLANDS AND NORTHWESTERN VALE BLM... WHICH ARE FIRE WEATHER ZONES 400...420...423...424...426...670... 671...672...673 AND 674"

            "headline": "Red Flag Warning issued June 25 at 11:42AM PDT until June 25 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS Pendleton OR",
            "description": "...Breezy winds and low relative humidity expected Today...\n\n.The combination of breezy winds and low relative humidity is\nexpected to generate weather conditions conducive to rapid fire\nspread for new and existing fires in the lower Columbia Basin,\nYakima and Kittitas valleys, and the Warm Springs and Yakama\nReservations.\n\n* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zone 703 Warm Springs Reservation.\n\n* TIMING...Until 8 PM PDT this evening.\n\n* WINDS...West 10 to 20 mph with gusts up to 30 mph.\n\n* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...10 to 20 percent.\n\n* IMPACTS...Any fire that develops will catch and spread\nquickly. Outdoor burning is not recommended.",
            "instruction": "A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions\nare either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of\nstrong winds, low relative humidity, and warm temperatures can\ncontribute to extreme fire behavior.",

            "senderName": "NWS Paducah KY",
            "headline": "Flood Watch issued June 25 at 1:17PM CDT until June 27 at 7:00AM CDT by NWS Paducah KY",
            "description": "* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.\n\n* WHERE...Portions of southeast Missouri, southern Illinois,\nsouthwest Indiana, and far northwest Kentucky.\n\n* WHEN...Through Saturday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,\ncreeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.\nLow-water crossings may be flooded.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- Multiple rounds of thunderstorms are expected through Friday\nnight. Repeated rounds of heavy rainfall from thunderstorms\ncould produce flash flooding.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood\nWarnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared\nto take action should flooding develop.",
            "response": "Prepare",

            "senderName": "NWS Hanford CA",
            "headline": "Red Flag Warning issued June 25 at 11:12AM PDT until June 27 at 11:00PM PDT by NWS Hanford CA",
            "description": "The National Weather Service in Hanford has issued a Red Flag\nWarning, which is in effect from 9 AM Friday to 11 PM PDT\nSaturday. The Fire Weather Watch is no longer in effect.\n\n\n* AFFECTED AREA...Fire weather zone Indian Wells Valley. Fire\nweather zone Kern County Desert. Fire weather zone Lake\nIsabella.\n\n* WIND...50 TO 60 PERCENT PROBABILITY OF GUSTS EXCEEDING 55 MPH ON\nFRIDAY IN EASTERN KERN COUNTY. 70 TO 80 PERCENT PROBABILITY OF\nGUSTS EXCEEDING 55 MPH ON SATURDAY IN EASTERN KERN COUNTY. 70 TO\n80 PERCENT PROBABILITY OF GUSTS EXCEEDING 30 MPH AT LAKE\nISABELLA.\n\n* HUMIDITY...EASTERN KERN COUNTY MINIMUM RELATIVE HUMIDITY\nBETWEEN 12-20 PERCENT. LAKE ISABELLA MINIMUM RELATIVE\nHUMIDITY BETWEEN 25-35 PERCENT.\n\n* THUNDERSTORMS...NO THUNDERSTORM THREAT\n\n* IMPACTS...any fires that develop will likely spread rapidly.\nOutdoor burning is not recommended.",
            "instruction": "A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions\nare either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of\nstrong winds, low relative humidity, and warm temperatures can\ncontribute to extreme fire behavior.",

            "senderName": "NWS Grand Junction CO",
            "headline": "Air Quality Alert issued June 25 at 12:10PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO",
            "description": "The Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment has\nissued the following...\n\nWHAT...Air Quality Health Advisory for Wildfire Smoke.\n\nWHERE...Moffat, Routt, Grand, Rio Blanco, Eagle, Summit, Garfield,\nPitkin, Mesa, Delta, Gunnison, Montrose, Saguache, Jackson, Lake,\nPark, Teller, Chaffee, Fremont, Custer, Huerfano, Rio Grande,\nAlamosa, Las Animas, Costilla and Conejos Counties. Locations\ninclude, but are not limited to Craig, Steamboat Springs, Granby,\nHot Sulphur Springs, Kremmling, Meeker, Rangely, Eagle, Vail,\nBreckenridge, Glenwood Springs, Aspen, Grand Junction, Delta,\nGunnison, Montrose, Nucla, Saguache, Walden, Leadville, Fairplay,\nCripple Creek, Buena Vista, Salida, Canon City, Westcliffe,\nWalsenburg, Del Norte, South Fork, Alamosa, Kim, Trinidad, San\nLuis and Conejos.\n\nWHEN...900 AM Thursday June 25 to 900 AM Friday June 26\n\nIMPACTS...Smoke from several fires burning in Utah and Nevada is\nbeing transported into Colorado and is expected to impact air\nquality through at least Thursday morning. Smoke levels could\nincrease or decrease rapidly at times during the advisory period\ndue to the very unstable atmospheric conditions.\n\nHEALTH INFORMATION...Public Health Recommendations: If smoke is\nthick or becomes thick in your neighborhood you may want to remain\nindoors. This is especially true for those with heart disease,\nrespiratory illnesses, the very young, and older adults. Consider\nlimiting outdoor activity when moderate to heavy smoke is present.\nConsider relocating temporarily if smoke is present indoors and is\nmaking you ill. If visibility is less than 5 miles in smoke in\nyour neighborhood, smoke has reached levels that are unhealthy.",
            "instruction": null,
            "response": "Monitor",
            "note": "Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.",

            "senderName": "NWS Pueblo CO",
            "headline": "Air Quality Alert issued June 25 at 12:10PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO",
            "description": "The Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment has\nissued the following...\n\nWHAT...Air Quality Health Advisory for Wildfire Smoke.\n\nWHERE...Moffat, Routt, Grand, Rio Blanco, Eagle, Summit, Garfield,\nPitkin, Mesa, Delta, Gunnison, Montrose, Saguache, Jackson, Lake,\nPark, Teller, Chaffee, Fremont, Custer, Huerfano, Rio Grande,\nAlamosa, Las Animas, Costilla and Conejos Counties. Locations\ninclude, but are not limited to Craig, Steamboat Springs, Granby,\nHot Sulphur Springs, Kremmling, Meeker, Rangely, Eagle, Vail,\nBreckenridge, Glenwood Springs, Aspen, Grand Junction, Delta,\nGunnison, Montrose, Nucla, Saguache, Walden, Leadville, Fairplay,\nCripple Creek, Buena Vista, Salida, Canon City, Westcliffe,\nWalsenburg, Del Norte, South Fork, Alamosa, Kim, Trinidad, San\nLuis and Conejos.\n\nWHEN...900 AM Thursday June 25 to 900 AM Friday June 26\n\nIMPACTS...Smoke from several fires burning in Utah and Nevada is\nbeing transported into Colorado and is expected to impact air\nquality through at least Thursday morning. Smoke levels could\nincrease or decrease rapidly at times during the advisory period\ndue to the very unstable atmospheric conditions.\n\nHEALTH INFORMATION...Public Health Recommendations: If smoke is\nthick or becomes thick in your neighborhood you may want to remain\nindoors. This is especially true for those with heart disease,\nrespiratory illnesses, the very young, and older adults. Consider\nlimiting outdoor activity when moderate to heavy smoke is present.\nConsider relocating temporarily if smoke is present indoors and is\nmaking you ill. If visibility is less than 5 miles in smoke in\nyour neighborhood, smoke has reached levels that are unhealthy.",
            "instruction": null,
            "response": "Monitor",
            "note": "Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.",

            "headline": "Winter Storm Watch issued June 25 at 11:56AM MDT until June 29 at 9:00AM MDT by NWS Missoula MT",
            "description": "* WHAT...Heavy wet snow possible above 6500 feet. Total snow\naccumulations up to 6 inches possible.\n\n* WHERE...Backcountry and higher elevation areas, including Williams\nCreek Summit.\n\n* WHEN...From Saturday evening through Monday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...Plan for winter-like conditions in the backcountry and\nhigher elevations. Cold temperatures and wet snow will elevate the\nrisk of hypothermia. Heavy wet snow may down trees, blocking access\nto backcountry roadways.",
            "instruction": "Monitor the latest forecasts for updates on this situation.\n\nPersons should consider delaying travel across high elevation\nbackcountry roadways. Consider taking a winter storm kit along with\nyou, including such items as tire chains, booster cables, flashlight,\nshovel, blankets and extra clothing. Also take water, a first aid\nkit, and anything else that would help you survive in case you become\nstranded.\n\nDo not touch downed lines and report any power outages to your\nelectric company. Travel is highly discouraged across backcountry\nroadways given the risk for downed trees to block roadways.",
            "response": "Prepare",
            "note": null,

            "event": "Flash Flood Watch",
            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Cheyenne WY",
            "headline": "Flash Flood Watch issued June 25 at 11:54AM MDT until June 26 at 12:00AM MDT by NWS Cheyenne WY",
            "description": "* WHAT...Flash flooding and debris flows caused by excessive\nrainfall continue to be possible over the South Fork Burn Scar\nArea.\n\n* WHERE...The South Fork Burn Scar Area in the northern Nebraska\npanhandle and downstream areas along Soldier Creek and the White\nRiver, including Fort Robinson and Crawford.\n\n* WHEN...Through this evening.\n\n* IMPACTS...Localized thunderstorm heavy rainfall over the South\nFork Burn Scar Area is possible. Multiple rounds of thunderstorms\nare expected in the area through Thursday evening. Residents near\nthe South Fork Burn Scar Area should prepare for potential\nflooding impacts. Be sure to stay up to date with information from\nlocal authorities. Heavy rainfall could trigger flash flooding of\nlow-lying areas, urbanized street flooding, and debris flows in\nand near recent wildfire burn scars.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- National Weather Service Meteorologists are forecasting\nlocally heavy rainfall over the burn scar, which may lead to\nflash flooding and debris flows.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action\nshould Flash Flood Warnings be issued.",
            "response": "Monitor",
            "note": null,

            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Dodge City KS",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 25 at 12:46PM CDT until June 26 at 8:00AM CDT by NWS Dodge City KS",
            "description": "* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.\n\n* WHERE...Portions of southwest and west central Kansas, including\nthe following counties, in southwest Kansas, Finney and Hodgeman.\nIn west central Kansas, Lane, Ness and Scott.\n\n* WHEN...Until 800 AM CDT Friday.\n\n* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying\nand flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Numerous roads\nremain closed due to flooding.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 1246 PM CDT, Emergency management in Lane county reported\nall roads and bridges south of highway 96 and north of\nhighway 96 in Dighton have inundated impassible roads.  1\nfarm stead has cut off road access and a washed out railroad\nbridge west of Dighton.\n- Radar rainfall estimates of 2 to 3+ inches of rain from the\nstorms this morning from Scott City to Dighton to northeast\nFinney county.\n- Some locations that will experience flooding include...\nScott City, Dighton, Alamota, Amy, Grigston, Manning, Healy,\nShallow Water, Scott State Lake and Modoc.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nMove to higher ground now. Act quickly to protect your life.",
            "response": "Avoid",
            "note": null,
            "parameters": {

              ],

            "event": "Red Flag Warning",
            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Flagstaff AZ",
            "headline": "Red Flag Warning issued June 25 at 10:41AM MST until June 28 at 8:00PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ",
            "description": "* WHAT...Critical fire weather conditions expected. Southwest winds\n15-25 mph, gusts to 40 mph Friday, southwest winds 20 to 30 mph\nwith gusts up to 50 mph Saturday and Sunday. Expect winds to remain\nelevated Saturday night. Relative humidity as low as 7 percent\ndesert areas, to 15-20 percent in forested locations.\n\n* WHERE...Kaibab Plateau, Marble and Glen Canyons, Grand Canyon\nCountry, Coconino Plateau, Yavapai County Mountains, Northeast\nPlateaus and Mesas Hwy 264 Northward, Chinle Valley, Chuska\nMountains and Defiance Plateau, Little Colorado River Valley in\nCoconino County, Little Colorado River Valley in Navajo County,\nLittle Colorado River Valley in Apache County, Western Mogollon\nRim, Eastern Mogollon Rim, White Mountains, Northern Gila County,\nYavapai County Valleys and Basins, Oak Creek and Sycamore Canyons,\nBlack Mesa Area, and Northeast Plateaus and Mesas South of Hwy 264.\nThis includes portions of the Apache-Sitgreaves, Coconino, Kaibab,\nPrescott, and Tonto national forests.\n\n* WHEN...From 11 AM MST /noon MDT/ Friday to 8 PM MST /9 PM MDT/\nSunday.\n\n* IMPACTS...Rapid spread and growth of any new or existing fires.\nFires will have the potential to exhibit extreme fire behavior.\nElevated potential for new fire starts. Winds may damage power\nlines resulting in new fire starts.",
            "instruction": "Do your part: No open flames or sparks, keep vehicles off of dry\ngrass, properly dispose of cigarette butts, and avoid power equipment\nthat creates sparks. One less spark, one less wildfire.\n\nObey all fire restrictions. To view a map of current fire\nrestrictions, go to wildlandfire.az.gov/fire-restrictions.\n\nA Red Flag Warning is issued when we identify weather conditions that\npromote rapid spread of fire which may become life-threatening. This\ndoes not mean there is a fire. These conditions are either occurring\nnow or will begin soon. It is important to have multiple ways to\nreceive information from authorities.\n\nPlease advise the appropriate officials or fire crews in the field of\nthis Red Flag Warning.",
            "response": "Prepare",
            "note": null,
            "parameters": {
              "AWIPSidentifier": [
                "RFWFGZ"
              ],
              "WMOidentifier": [
                "WWUS85 KFGZ 251741"
              ],

            "senderName": "NWS Dodge City KS",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 25 at 12:29PM CDT until June 26 at 10:00PM CDT by NWS Dodge City KS",
            "description": "...The National Weather Service in Dodge City KS has issued a Flood\nWarning for the following rivers in Kansas...\n\nSouth Fork Ninnescah River near Pratt affecting Pratt County.\n\nFor the SF Ninnescah River...including Pratt...Minor flooding is\nforecast.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...South Fork Ninnescah River near Pratt.\n\n* WHEN...From this afternoon to late tomorrow evening.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 9.0 feet, Expect overflow of banks. Stream overflows\nnarrowly on the left bank and more broadly on the right bank.\nStream is approximately 260 ft wide at this stage.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 10:00 AM CDT Thursday the stage was 4.3 feet.\n- Bankfull stage is 5.0 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage\nlate this afternoon to a crest of 9.1 feet this evening. It\nwill then fall below flood stage late this evening.\n- Flood stage is 9.0 feet.\n- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of\n9.1 feet on 10/04/2002.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.\n\nThe next statement will be issued late tonight at 1230 AM CDT.",

            "description": "* WHAT...For today, west winds 15 to 25 mph with gusts up to 35 mph\nfor Pyramid Lake, Lahontan, and Rye Patch Reservoirs. Wave heights\n1 to 3 feet on Pyramid Lake.             "headline": "Red Flag Warning issued June 25 at 11:08AM MDT until June 26 at 9:00PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO",
            "description": "...RED FLAG WARNING IN EFFECT FROM 10 AM SATURDAY TO MIDNIGHT MDT\nSATURDAY NIGHT FOR GUSTY WINDS, LOW RELATIVE HUMIDITY AND DRY\nFUELS FOR FIRE WEATHER ZONE 203 BELOW 8000 FEET...\n\n...FIRE WEATHER WATCH IN EFFECT FROM SUNDAY AFTERNOON THROUGH\nSUNDAY EVENING FOR GUSTY WINDS, LOW RELATIVE HUMIDITY AND DRY\nFUELS FOR FIRE WEATHER ZONE 203...\n\nThe National Weather Service in Grand Junction has issued a Red\nFlag Warning below 8000 feet for gusty winds, low relative\nhumidity and dry fuels, which is in effect from 10 AM Saturday to\nmidnight MDT Saturday night.             "description": "...RED FLAG WARNING IN EFFECT FROM 10 AM SATURDAY TO MIDNIGHT MDT\nSATURDAY NIGHT FOR GUSTY WINDS, LOW RELATIVE HUMIDITY AND DRY\nFUELS FOR FIRE WEATHER ZONES 202, 207, AND 290...\n\n...FIRE WEATHER WATCH IN EFFECT FROM SUNDAY AFTERNOON THROUGH\nSUNDAY EVENING FOR GUSTY WINDS, LOW RELATIVE HUMIDITY AND DRY\nFUELS FOR FIRE WEATHER ZONES 202, 207, AND 290...\n\nThe National Weather Service in Grand Junction has issued a Red\nFlag Warning for gusty winds, low relative humidity and dry\nfuels, which is in effect from 10 AM Saturday to midnight MDT\nSaturday night.             "headline": "Fire Weather Watch issued June 25 at 10:04AM PDT until June 27 at 11:00PM PDT by NWS Elko NV",
            "description": "The National Weather Service in Elko has issued a Red Flag\nWarning, which is in effect from 11 AM to 11 PM PDT Friday. A Fire\nWeather Watch has also been issued.             "instruction": "A red flag warning means that critical fire weather conditions\nare either occurring now, or will shortly.             "description": "The National Weather Service in Fairbanks has issued a Red Flag\nWarning for lightning, which is in effect from noon today to\nmidnight AKDT Friday morning.\n\n* AFFECTED AREA...Upper Koyukuk Valley.\n\n* TIMING...From 12 PM Thursday to 12 AM Friday.\n\n* THUNDERSTORM COVERAGE INDEX...Scattered\n\n* WINDS...West 5 to 10 mph.\n\n* HUMIDITY...As low as 28 percent.\n\n* TEMPERATURES...Highs in the low to mid 80s.\n\n* IMPACTS...Critical fire weather conditions are expected due to\nscattered thunderstorms. Thunderstorms will come with frequent\nlightning this afternoon into the overnight. Any lightning can\ncause new ignitions since the fuels are dry and burnable.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Most of the thunderstorm activity will move\nout of the region by 12 AM Friday morning. If we notice the\nthunderstorm risk is ending earlier, we will act as necessary.",

            "description": "* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be\npossible.\n\n* WHERE...Portions of central, east central, north central, and\nnortheast Kansas, including the following counties, in central\nKansas, Dickinson. In northeast Kansas,\nJefferson.\n\n* WHEN...Through Friday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,\ncreeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.\nCreeks and streams may rise out of their banks.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- Thunderstorms with very heavy rainfall are likely this\nafternoon through tomorrow morning. Widespread one to two\ninches of rainfall is likely, with isolated higher amounts\npossible.",

            "event": "Air Quality Alert",
            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Phoenix AZ",
            "headline": "Air Quality Alert issued June 25 at 8:35AM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ",
            "description": "* WHAT...The Imperial County APCD has issued an air quality alert\ndue to harmful levels of particle pollution from windblown dust.\nVisit https://www.aqmd.gov/alertinfo to check current and forecasted\nair quality levels.\n\n* WHERE...the Imperial Valley. Levels of particle pollution can vary\nby time and location depending on emissions and local weather\nconditions.\n\n* WHEN...from 2 PM Friday, June 26, 2026 through 11:59 PM Saturday,\nJune 27, 2026.\n\n* IMPACTS... Particle pollution can get deep into the lungs and\ncause serious health problems such as asthma attacks, heart and lung\ndisease symptoms, and increased risk of lung infections. Everyone\ncan be affected, but sensitive groups such as people with lung or\nheart disease, older adults, people who are pregnant, children, and\nthose who spend a lot of time outdoors are at greater risk.",
            "instruction": "To protect your health, check air quality levels and act as needed:\n\n* When Air Quality Index (AQI) levels are \"Unhealthy for\nSensitive Groups\" (orange), sensitive groups as specified\nabove should limit extended or intense outdoor activity.\n* When AQI is \"Unhealthy\" (red), everyone may experience health\nimpacts. Sensitive groups should avoid extended time outdoors.\n* When AQI is \"Very Unhealthy\" (purple), sensitive groups should\navoid all outdoor physical activity. Everyone else should\navoid extended or intense outdoor activity.\n* When AQI is \"Hazardous\" (maroon), everyone should avoid all\noutdoor physical activity.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n\nTo help keep indoor air clean when air quality is poor:\n\n* Keep windows and doors closed\n* Run your air conditioner and/or an air purifier\n* Do not use whole house fans or swamp coolers that bring in\noutside air if you have other methods to stay cool\n* Avoid other sources of pollution such as fireplaces, candles,\nincense, grilling, and gasoline-powered lawn and garden\nequipment\n\nTo help minimize outdoor particle pollution levels:\n\n* Carpool, telecommute, reduce trips, or take public\ntransportation\n* Slow down if driving on dirt roads\n* Stabilize loose soils",
            "response": "Monitor",
            "note": "Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.",
