            "event": "Flood Warning",
            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Lincoln IL",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 25 at 10:17AM CDT by NWS Lincoln IL",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in\nIllinois...\n\nLittle Wabash River below Clay City affecting Clay and Richland\nCounties.\n\n.The following forecasts are based on observed precipitation, soil\nmoisture conditions, and forecast precipitation.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Little Wabash River below Clay City.\n\n* WHEN...Until further notice.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 22.0 feet, North Clay Road...1 mile east of the gage\nis flooded.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 9:45 AM CDT Thursday the stage was 20.7 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours\nending at 9:45 AM CDT Thursday was 21.0 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 21.4\nfeet Sunday evening.\n- Flood stage is 18.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Persons with interests along this river need to remain aware of the\nlatest forecasts and associated flood risk for their area. Stay\ntuned for further updates on this flooding situation.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.",
            "response": "Avoid",
            "note": null,

            "sender": "w-nws.webmaster@noaa.gov",
            "senderName": "NWS Denver CO",
            "headline": "Air Quality Alert issued June 25 at 9:10AM MDT by NWS Denver CO",
            "description": "The Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment has\nissued the following...\n\nWHAT...Air Quality Health Advisory for Wildfire Smoke.\n\nWHERE...Moffat, Routt, Grand, Rio Blanco, Eagle, Summit, Garfield,\nPitkin, Mesa, Delta, Gunnison, Montrose, Jackson, Lake, Park,\nTeller, Chaffee, Custer, Huerfano, Rio Grande, Alamosa, Las\nAnimas, Costilla, Conejos, Saguache and Fremont Counties.\nLocations include, but are not limited to Craig, Steamboat\nSprings, Granby, Hot Sulphur Springs, Kremmling, Meeker, Rangely,\nEagle, Vail, Breckenridge, Glenwood Springs, Aspen, Grand\nJunction, Delta, Gunnison, Montrose, Nucla, Walden, Leadville,\nFairplay, Cripple Creek, Buena Vista, Salida, Westcliffe,\nWalsenburg, Del Norte, South Fork, Alamosa, Kim, Trinidad, San\nLuis, Conejos, Saguache and Canon City.\n\nWHEN...900 AM Thursday June 25 to 900 AM Friday June 26\n\nIMPACTS...Smoke from several fires burning in Utah and Nevada is\nbeing transported into Colorado and is expected to impact air\nquality through at least Thursday morning. Smoke levels could\nincrease or decrease rapidly at times during the advisory period\ndue to the very unstable atmospheric conditions.\n\nHEALTH INFORMATION...Public Health Recommendations: If smoke is\nthick or becomes thick in your neighborhood you may want to remain\nindoors. This is especially true for those with heart disease,\nrespiratory illnesses, the very young, and older adults. Consider\nlimiting outdoor activity when moderate to heavy smoke is present.\nConsider relocating temporarily if smoke is present indoors and is\nmaking you ill. If visibility is less than 5 miles in smoke in\nyour neighborhood, smoke has reached levels that are unhealthy.",

            "response": "Monitor",

            "senderName": "NWS Chicago IL",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 25 at 9:58AM CDT until June 29 at 7:00AM CDT by NWS Chicago IL",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in\nIllinois...\n\nIllinois River at La Salle affecting Bureau, La Salle and Putnam\nCounties.\n\n...The Flood Warning is cancelled for the following rivers in\nIllinois...\n\nThorn Creek at Thornton affecting Cook County.\n\nFor the Illinois River (Upper)...including La Salle...Minor flooding\nis forecast.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Illinois River from Starved Rock Lock and Dam downstream\nto confluence with Big Bureau Creek, including the La Salle gauge.\n\n* WHEN...Until Monday morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 22.0 feet, Lower parking lot at Starved Rock State\nPark is inundated east of La Salle. High water levels begin to\nimpact shipping interests along the river.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 9:45 AM CDT Thursday the stage was 22.0 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage\nearly Monday morning and continue falling to 18.3 feet\nThursday, July 02.\n- Flood stage is 20.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "A Flood Warning means water levels above flood stage are imminent or\nmay already be occurring. Persons along rivers and streams in the\nwarned area should take immediate precautions to protect life and\nproperty.\n\nThese forecasts are based on observed precipitation as well as\nforecast precipitation 24 hours into the future. Changes to the\nrainfall forecast, or any additional rainfall after 24 hours, may\ncause changes to these river forecasts.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.\n\nThe next statement will be issued by this morning.",

            "senderName": "NWS Paducah KY",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 25 at 9:56AM CDT until July 2 at 9:00PM CDT by NWS Paducah KY",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in\nIllinois...Indiana...\n\nWabash River at New Harmony\n\n.Minor flooding continues along the Wabash River at New Harmony. The\nriver is forecast to near 16.3 feet Sunday afternoon and then fall\nbelow flood stage Thursday, July 2nd.\n\nFor the Wabash River...including New Harmony...Minor flooding is\nforecast.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Wabash River at New Harmony.\n\n* WHEN...Until Thursday, July 02.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 15.0 feet, The river overflows low ground on the\nIllinois side.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 9:30 AM CDT Thursday the stage was 15.1 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 16.3\nfeet early Sunday afternoon. It will then fall below flood\nstage Thursday, July 02.\n- Flood stage is 15.0 feet.\n- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of\n16.3 feet on 04/23/1993.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.",
            "response": "Avoid",

            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 25 at 9:53AM CDT by NWS Paducah KY",
            "description": "...The National Weather Service in Paducah KY has issued a Flood\nWarning for the following rivers in Illinois...\n\nLittle Wabash River at Carmi\n\n.Forecast heavy rain is expected to bring minor flooding to the\nLittle Wabash River at Carmi. The river is expected to rise above\nflood stage on Sunday and stage above flood stage until further\nnotice.\n\nFor the Little Wabash River...including Carmi...Minor flooding is\nforecast.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Little Wabash River at Carmi.\n\n* WHEN...From late Saturday night until further notice.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 32.0 feet, Flood waters flow up McHenry slough and\nareas near Route 1 and 14 in Carmi begin to flood.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 9:30 AM CDT Thursday the stage was 13.3 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage\nearly Sunday morning and continue rising to 30.5 feet\nThursday, July 02. Additional rises are possible thereafter.\n- Flood stage is 27.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov.",

            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 25 at 9:43AM CDT by NWS St Louis MO",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in\nIllinois...\n\nIllinois River at Meredosia.\n\nIllinois River at La Grange LD.\n\nIllinois River at Valley City.\n\nIllinois River at Hardin.\n\nRiver forecasts are based on observed precipitation and forecast\nprecipitation for the next 24 hours.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Illinois River at Meredosia.\n\n* WHEN...Until further notice.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 21.0 feet, Chambers Road south of Naples floods at\nMauvaise Terre Creek near this level.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 9:30 AM CDT Thursday the stage was 19.8 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending\nat 9:30 AM CDT Thursday was 19.8 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 20.6 feet\ntomorrow evening.\n- Flood stage is 17.0 feet.",
            "instruction": "Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars\nthrough flooded areas.\n\nThis product, along with additional weather and stream information,\nis available at https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/lsx",

            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 25 at 9:43AM CDT by NWS St Louis MO",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in\nIllinois...\n\nIllinois River at Meredosia.\n\nIllinois River at La Grange LD.\n\nIllinois River at Valley City.\n\nIllinois River at Hardin.\n\nRiver forecasts are based on observed precipitation and forecast\nprecipitation for the next 24 hours.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Illinois River at Hardin.\n\n* WHEN...Until further notice.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 9:30 AM CDT Thursday the stage was 26.9 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending\nat 9:30 AM CDT Thursday was 26.9 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 27.0 feet\nthis evening.\n- Flood stage is 25.0 feet.",
            "instruction": "Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars\nthrough flooded areas.\n\nThis product, along with additional weather and stream information,\nis available at https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/lsx",
            "response": "Avoid",
            "note": null,

            "senderName": "NWS Houston/Galveston TX",
            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 25 at 9:12AM CDT until June 26 at 11:00AM CDT by NWS Houston/Galveston TX",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Texas...\n\nNavasota River near Normangee affecting Madison, Brazos and\nGrimes Counties.\n\nFor the Navasota River...including Normangee...Minor flooding is\nforecast.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Navasota River near Normangee.\n\n* WHEN...Until late tomorrow morning.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 15.0 feet, Minor lowland flooding begins as water\nescapes the main channel and inundates the floodplain.\nAt 17.0 feet, Minor lowland flooding continues with widespread\ninundation of the floodplain in the vicinity of the gage with the\nriver more than 1 mile wide. Long Trussel Road in northeast Brazos\nCounty below State Highway 21 is threatened.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 8:00 AM CDT Thursday the stage was 15.1 feet.\n- Bankfull stage is 12.0 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours\nending at 8:00 AM CDT Thursday was 15.8 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage\nthis afternoon and continue falling to 6.7 feet Tuesday\nmorning.\n- Flood stage is 15.0 feet.\n- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of\n15.2 feet on 05/22/2015.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood\ndeaths occur in vehicles.\n\nMotorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive\ncars through flooded areas.\n\nAdditional information is available at www.weather.gov/hgx.\n\nThe next statement will be issued by Friday morning at 1100 AM CDT.",
            "response": "Avoid",
            "note": null,

            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 25 at 8:56AM CDT by NWS Shreveport LA",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in\nArkansas...Louisiana...\n\nBayou Dorcheat Near Springhill affecting Webster and Columbia\nParishes.\n\nFor the Bayou Dorcheat...including Springhill...Minor flooding is\nforecast.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Bayou Dorcheat near Springhill.\n\n* WHEN...Until further notice.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 13.0 feet, Minor lowland flooding of private boat\nramps. Move livestock to higher ground.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 8:00 AM CDT Thursday the stage was 13.6 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 14.0 feet\nFriday evening.\n- Flood stage is 11.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Do not drive cars through flooded areas. Caution is urged when\nwalking near riverbanks. Turn around, don't drown when encountering\nflooded roads. Most flood deaths occur in vehicles.\n\nFor more hydrologic information, copy and paste the following website\naddress into your favorite web browser URL bar:\nhttps://water.noaa.gov/wfo/SHV\n\nThe next statement will be issued Friday morning at 900 AM CDT.",
            "response": "Avoid",

            "headline": "Flood Warning issued June 25 at 8:55AM CDT until June 30 at 4:00PM CDT by NWS Shreveport LA",
            "description": "...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in\nLouisiana...\n\nBayou D'Arbonne At Lake D'Arbonne affecting Union Parish.\n\nFor the Bayou D'arbonne...including Lake D'Arbonne...Minor flooding\nis forecast.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Bayou D'Arbonne at Lake D'Arbonne.\n\n* WHEN...From Saturday morning to Tuesday afternoon.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 83.0 feet, Expect flooding of secondary roadways with\nsome camps suffering overflow. Boats should be moved from\nboathouses to prevent damage to boats and boathouses, otherwise\nboats may actually rise through the roofs of boathouses with the\nhigh water.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 7:45 AM CDT Thursday the stage was 81.6 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage\nSaturday morning to a crest of 83.5 feet Sunday morning. It will\nthen fall below flood stage late Monday evening.\n- Flood stage is 83.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Do not drive cars through flooded areas. Caution is urged when\nwalking near riverbanks. Turn around, don't drown when encountering\nflooded roads. Most flood deaths occur in vehicles.\n\nFor more hydrologic information, copy and paste the following website\naddress into your favorite web browser URL bar:\nhttps://water.noaa.gov/wfo/SHV\n\nThe next statement will be issued Friday morning at 900 AM CDT.",

            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in\nLouisiana...\n\nBayou D'arbonne At Lake Claiborne affecting Claiborne Parish.\n\nFor the Bayou D'arbonne...including Lake Claiborne...Minor flooding\nis forecast.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Bayou D'arbonne at Lake Claiborne.\n\n* WHEN...Until Friday evening.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 187.5 feet, Expect flooding of some camps.             "senderName": "NWS Dodge City KS",
            "headline": "Flood Watch issued June 25 at 8:17AM CDT until June 26 at 1:00AM CDT by NWS Dodge City KS",
            "description": "Scattered to numerous thunderstorms will continue Thursday into\nThursday night. Some storms will produce excessive rainfall on soils\nalready saturated from previous rains, with continued runoff\nconcerns.\n\n* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be\npossible.\n\n* WHERE...Portions of central, south central, southwest, and west\ncentral Kansas, including the following counties, in central\nKansas, Ellis and Rush. In south central Kansas, Barber, Comanche,\nEdwards, Kiowa, Pawnee, Pratt and Stafford. In southwest Kansas,\nClark, Finney, Ford, Grant, Gray, Hamilton, Haskell, Hodgeman,\nKearny, Meade, Morton, Seward, Stanton and Stevens. In west\ncentral Kansas, Lane, Ness, Scott and Trego.\n\n* WHEN...Through late tonight.\n\n* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,\ncreeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.\nFlooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Area creeks\nand streams are running high and could flood with more heavy rain.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action\nshould Flash Flood Warnings be issued.",
            "response": "Prepare",
            "note": null,

            "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...\n\nNeches River Near Diboll affecting Trinity, Polk and Angelina\nCounties.\n\nFor the Neches River...including Diboll...Minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Neches River near Diboll.\n\n* WHEN...From Friday afternoon to late Saturday night.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 12.0 feet, Minor lowland flooding occurs.  Expect\nflooded boat ramps and trails.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 7:15 AM CDT Thursday the stage was 11.1 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage early\ntomorrow afternoon to a crest of 12.1 feet early Saturday\nmorning. It will then fall below flood stage Saturday morning.\n- Flood stage is 12.0 feet.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
            "instruction": "Do not drive cars through flooded areas. Caution is urged when\nwalking near riverbanks. Turn around, don't drown when encountering\nflooded roads. Most flood deaths occur in vehicles.\n\nFor more hydrologic information, copy and paste the following website\naddress into your favorite web browser URL bar:\nhttps://water.noaa.gov/wfo/SHV\n\nThe next statement will be issued Friday morning at 745 AM CDT.",

            "senderName": "NWS Goodland KS",
            "headline": "Flood Watch issued June 25 at 5:45AM MDT until June 26 at 12:00AM MDT by NWS Goodland KS",
            "description": "Multiple days of heavy rainfall has led to saturated soil across\nmuch of the Tri-State area. Additional rainfall is expected today\nand could lead to flash flooding.\n\n* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be\npossible.\n\n* WHERE...Portions of Colorado, including the following areas, Kit\nCarson and Yuma, Kansas, including the following areas, Cheyenne\nKS, Decatur, Gove, Graham, Greeley, Logan, Norton, Rawlins,\nSheridan, Sherman, Thomas, Wallace and Wichita, and southwest\nNebraska, including the following areas, Dundy, Hitchcock and Red\nWillow.\n\n* WHEN...Through this evening.\n\n* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in additional flooding of\nrivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone\nlocations. Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.\nLow-water crossings may be flooded. Extensive street flooding and\nflooding of creeks and rivers are possible. Area creeks and\nstreams are running high and could flood with more heavy rain.",
            "instruction": "You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action\nshould Flash Flood Warnings be issued.",
            "response": "Prepare",
            "note": null,

            "senderName": "NWS Midland/Odessa TX",
            "headline": "Heat Advisory issued June 25 at 12:50AM CDT until June 25 at 9:00PM CDT by NWS Midland/Odessa TX",
            "description": "* WHAT...Temperatures up to 113 expected.\n\n* WHERE...Lower Brewster County, Presidio Valley, and Rio Grande\nValley.\n\n* WHEN...From 2 PM this afternoon to 9 PM CDT this evening.\n\n* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures may cause heat illnesses. Extreme heat\nwill significantly increase the potential for heat related\nillnesses, particularly for those working or participating in\noutdoor activities.",
            "instruction": "Drink plenty of fluids even if you don't feel thirsty, but avoid\nalcohol and caffeine. Stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of\nthe sun, and check up on elderly and vulnerable relatives and\nneighbors.\n\nTo reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and\nHealth Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in\nshaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat\nshould be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an\nemergency! Call 9 1 1.\n\nLook before you lock! Do not leave young children and pets in\nunattended vehicles for even a moment. Car interiors will very\nquickly reach lethal temperatures.",
            "response": "Execute",
            "note": null,
            "parameters": {
